title.zh: 卷九十八 列傳第八十六: 蠕蠕 匈奴宇文莫槐 徒何段就六眷 高車
title.en: Volume 98 Biographies 86: Rouran, Yuwen Mohuai Xiongnu, Duanliu Liujuan, Gaoche
title.raw: 卷九十八 列傳第八十六: 蠕蠕 匈奴宇文莫槐 徒何段就六眷 高車 Volume 98 Biographies 86: Rouran, Yuwen Mohuai Xiongnu, Duanliu Liujuan, Gaoche

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕 匈奴宇文莫槐 徒何段就六眷 高車

translations.literal: Rouran; Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu; Duan Jiuliujuan of the Tuge; Gaoche
translations.idiomatic: Rouran; Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu; Duan Jiuliujuan of the Tuge; and the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 列傳第八十六蠕蠕匈奴宇文莫槐徒何段就六眷高車

translations.literal: Biography 86: Rouran, Yuwen Mohuai Xiongnu, Duan Jiuliujuan Tuge, Gaoche
translations.idiomatic: Biography 86: the Rouran, Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu, Duan Jiuliujuan of the Tuge, and the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕姓鬱久閭氏。

translations.literal: The Rouran bore the clan name Yujiuli.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran people took the clan name Yujiuli.

sentences.zh: 始神元之末，掠騎有得一奴，發始齊眉，忘本姓名，其主字之曰木骨閭。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Shenyuan's reign, raiding horsemen captured a slave whose hair had only grown to his eyebrows; he had forgotten his original name, and his master gave him the courtesy name Mugulü.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Shenyuan's reign, a raiding party seized a slave whose hair had barely reached his brows; he no longer remembered his own name, and his master styled him Mugulü.

sentences.zh: 「木骨閭」者，首禿也。

translations.literal: "Mugulü" means "bald head."
translations.idiomatic: Mugulü means "bald head."

sentences.zh: 「木骨閭」與「鬱久閭」聲相近，故後子孫因以為氏。

translations.literal: "Mugulü" and "Yujiuli" sound similar; therefore later descendants adopted it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Because "Mugulü" and "Yujiuli" sound alike, later generations took it as their clan name.

sentences.zh: 木骨閭既壯，免奴為騎卒。

translations.literal: When Mugulü came of age, he was freed from slavery and became a cavalry soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mugulü had grown strong, he was released from bondage and enrolled as a mounted trooper.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，坐後期當斬，亡匿廣漠谿穀間，收合逋逃，得百餘人，依純突鄰部。

translations.literal: During Emperor Mu's reign, sentenced to death for lateness, he fled and hid in ravines of the vast desert, gathered fugitives, obtained more than a hundred men, and attached himself to the Chuntuolin tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu he was condemned to death for arriving late; he vanished into the gullies of the deep desert, rallied runaways until he had more than a hundred followers, and threw in his lot with the Chuntuolin tribe.

sentences.zh: 木骨閭死，子車鹿會雄健，始有部眾，自號柔然。

translations.literal: When Mugulü died, his son Cheluhui, strong and valiant, first gathered a tribal following and styled himself Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: After Mugulü's death his son Cheluhui, a man of great strength, first mustered a tribal following and called himself Rouran.

sentences.zh: 後太武以其無知，狀類於蟲，故改其號為蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Taiwu, deeming them ignorant and worm-like in appearance, changed their designation to Ruru.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taiwu, judging them stupid and worm-like in their ways, renamed them Ruru—"writhing worms."

sentences.zh: 車鹿會既為部帥，歲貢馬畜、貂豽皮。

translations.literal: Once Cheluhui became tribal chief, he annually presented tribute of horses, livestock, and sable and ferret pelts.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheluhui became chief of the tribe, each year he sent tribute of horses, herds, and sable and ferret furs.

sentences.zh: 冬則徙度漠南，夏則還居漠北。

translations.literal: In winter they migrated south across the desert; in summer they returned to dwell north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they crossed south of the desert; in summer they moved back to the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 車鹿會死，子吐奴傀立。

translations.literal: Cheluhui died; his son Tunugui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheluhui died, his son Tunugui took his place.

sentences.zh: 吐奴傀死，子跋提立。

translations.literal: Tunugui died; his son Bati succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tunugui died and was succeeded by his son Bati.

sentences.zh: 跋提死，子地粟袁立。

translations.literal: Bati died; his son Disuyuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Bati died and was succeeded by his son Disuyuan.

sentences.zh: 地粟袁死，其部分為二。

translations.literal: When Disuyuan died, his tribe split in two.
translations.idiomatic: After Disuyuan's death the tribe divided into two parts.

sentences.zh: 地粟袁長子匹候跋繼父，居東邊；

translations.literal: Disuyuan's eldest son Pihouba succeeded his father and dwelt in the east;
translations.idiomatic: Disuyuan's eldest son Pihouba inherited his father's position and settled in the east;

sentences.zh: 次子縕紇提，別居西邊。

translations.literal: the second son Wenhadi established a separate encampment in the west.
translations.idiomatic: the younger son Wenhadi broke away and lived apart in the west.

sentences.zh: 及昭成崩，縕紇提附衛辰而貳于魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaocheng died, Wenhadi attached himself to Wei Chen and turned disloyal toward Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaocheng passed away, Wenhadi leaned on Wei Chen and turned against Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏登國中討之，蠕蠕移部遁走，追之及于大磧南床山下，大破之，虜其半部。

translations.literal: During Wei's Dengguo campaign against him, the Rouran moved their tribes and fled; pursued to south of the great desert at Nanchuang Mountain, they suffered a great defeat and half the tribe was captured.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Dengguo punitive campaign the Rouran shifted their camps and fled; pursued to Nanchuang Mountain south of the great desert, they were routed and half the tribe was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 匹候跋及部帥屋擊，各收餘落遁走。

translations.literal: Pihouba and the tribal chief Wuji each gathered the remnant bands and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pihouba and the tribal chief Wuji each rallied what was left of their people and escaped.

sentences.zh: 遣長孫嵩及長孫肥追之，度磧。

translations.literal: [Wei] sent Changsun Song and Changsun Fei in pursuit, crossing the desert.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Changsun Song and Changsun Fei in pursuit, and they crossed the desert.

sentences.zh: 嵩至平望川，大破屋擊，禽之，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Song reached Pingwang River, routed Wuji greatly, captured him, and executed him as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Song reached the Pingwang River, crushed Wuji's forces, seized him, and beheaded him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 肥至涿邪山，及匹候跋，舉落請降。

translations.literal: Fei reached Zhuoyeshan, overtook Pihouba, and the entire tribe surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fei came to Zhuoyeshan, caught up with Pihouba, and the whole tribe submitted.

sentences.zh: 獲縕紇提子曷多汗及曷多汗兄誥歸之、社侖、斛律等，並宗黨數百人，分配諸部。

translations.literal: They captured Wenhadi's son Heduohan and Heduohan's elder brothers Gaoguizhi, Shelun, Hulü, and several hundred clansmen, distributing them among various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: They took Wenhadi's son Heduohan, together with his elder brothers Gaoguizhi, Shelun, Hulü, and several hundred kinsmen, and parcelled them out among the other tribes.

sentences.zh: 縕紇提西遁，將歸衛辰。

translations.literal: Wenhadi fled west, intending to join Wei Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhadi fled westward, planning to rejoin Wei Chen.

sentences.zh: 道武追之至跋那山，縕紇提復降，道武撫慰如舊。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu pursued him to Banashan; Wenhadi surrendered again, and Daowu comforted him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu pursued him to Banashan; Wenhadi submitted once more, and Daowu treated him with the same favor as before.

sentences.zh: 九年，曷多汗與社侖率部眾棄其父西走，長孫肥輕騎追之，至上郡跋那山，斬曷多汗，盡殆其眾，社侖數人奔匹候跋，匹候跋處之南鄙，去其庭五百里，令其子四人監之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Heduohan and Shelun led their tribes westward, abandoning their father; Changsun Fei with light cavalry pursued them to Banashan in Shang Commandery, slew Heduohan, and nearly exterminated their forces; Shelun and a few men fled to Pihouba, who settled them on the southern marches five hundred li from his court, placing his four sons to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Heduohan and Shelun led their followers west, deserting their father; Changsun Fei with light horse pursued them to Banashan in Shang Commandery, killed Heduohan, and all but wiped out their band. Shelun and a handful of men reached Pihouba, who lodged them on his southern border five hundred li from his headquarters and set four of his sons to watch them.

sentences.zh: 既而社侖率其私屬，執匹候跋四子而叛，襲匹候跋。

translations.literal: Before long Shelun led his private followers, seized Pihouba's four sons, rebelled, and attacked Pihouba.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shelun rallied his personal retainers, seized Pihouba's four sons, rebelled, and struck at Pihouba.

sentences.zh: 諸子收餘眾，亡依高車斛律部。

translations.literal: The sons gathered remnant forces and fled to take refuge with the Gaoche Hulü tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The sons rallied the survivors and fled for protection to the Gaoche Hulü tribe.

sentences.zh: 社侖凶狡有權變，月餘，乃釋匹候跋，歸其諸子，欲聚而殲之。

translations.literal: Shelun was fierce, cunning, and resourceful; after more than a month he released Pihouba and returned his sons, intending to gather them and annihilate them.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun was brutal, crafty, and full of stratagems; after a month or more he freed Pihouba and sent back his sons, planning to draw them together and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 密舉兵襲匹候跋，殺匹候跋。

translations.literal: Secretly he raised troops and attacked Pihouba, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he mobilized his men, fell upon Pihouba, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 子啟拔、吳頡等十五人，歸於道武。

translations.literal: Sons Qiba, Wuxie, and fifteen others went over to Emperor Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Qiba, Wuxie, and fifteen others defected to Emperor Daowu.

sentences.zh: 社侖既殺匹候跋，懼王師討之，乃掠五原以西諸部，北度大漠。

translations.literal: After Shelun killed Pihouba, fearing imperial punishment, he raided tribes west of Wuyuan and crossed the great desert to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shelun had killed Pihouba, dreading an imperial expedition, he plundered the tribes west of Wuyuan and crossed the great desert to the north.

sentences.zh: 道武以拔、頡為安遠將軍，平棘侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu appointed Qiba and Wuxie General of Pacifying the Distance and Marquis of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu made Qiba and Wuxie Generals of Pacifying the Distance and enfeoffed them as Marquises of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 社侖與姚興和親，道武遣材官將軍和突襲黜弗、素古延諸部，社侖遣騎素古延，突逆擊破之。

translations.literal: Shelun allied with Yao Xing by marriage; Emperor Daowu sent Material Works General He Tu to strike the Chufu and Suguoyan tribes; Shelun sent cavalry to rescue Suguoyan, and Tu counterattacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun sealed a marriage alliance with Yao Xing; Emperor Daowu sent Material Works General He Tu to raid the Chufu and Suguoyan tribes. Shelun dispatched horsemen to relieve Suguoyan, but Tu met them head-on and broke their force.

sentences.zh: 社侖遠遁漠北，侵高車，深入其地，遂並諸部，凶勢益振。

translations.literal: Shelun fled far into the northern desert, invaded the Gaoche, penetrated deep into their territory, then subsumed all their tribes; his ferocious power grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun withdrew deep into the northern wastes, attacked the Gaoche, drove far into their lands, and absorbed tribe after tribe until his savage might swelled without check.

sentences.zh: 北徙弱洛水，始立軍法；

translations.literal: Moving north to Ruoluo River, he first established military regulations;
translations.idiomatic: He shifted north to the Ruoluo River and for the first time imposed military law;

sentences.zh: 千人為軍，軍置將一人；

translations.literal: a thousand men formed an army, and each army had one general appointed;
translations.idiomatic: every thousand men made an army, and each army had one commander;

sentences.zh: 百人為幢，幢置帥一人。

translations.literal: a hundred men formed a banner company, and each company had one commander appointed.
translations.idiomatic: every hundred men made a banner, and each banner had one captain.

sentences.zh: 先登者賜以虜獲，退懦者以石擊首殺之，或臨時垂撻。

translations.literal: Those who charged first received spoils of captives; cowards who retreated were killed by stoning, or were flogged on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever led the assault received the captives as reward; anyone who hung back was stoned to death, or beaten on the spot.

sentences.zh: 無文記，將帥以羊屎粗討兵數，後頗知刻木為記。

translations.literal: They kept no written records; generals roughly reckoned troop numbers with sheep dung, and only later learned to keep accounts by carving wood.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing: commanders roughly tallied soldiers with pellets of sheep dung, and only later learned to keep track by notching wood.

sentences.zh: 其西北有匈奴余種，國尤富強，部帥日拔也稽舉兵擊社侖。

translations.literal: To their northwest were remnant bands of the Xiongnu, a state especially rich and strong; the tribal chief Riboyeji raised troops to attack Shelun.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of them lived Xiongnu remnants, a people unusually rich and strong; their chief Riboyeji took the field against Shelun.

sentences.zh: 逆戰於頞根河，大破之。

translations.literal: Meeting in battle at the Egen River, [Shelun] routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun met them on the Egen River and shattered them completely.

sentences.zh: 後盡為社侖所並。

translations.literal: Later they were all absorbed by Shelun.
translations.idiomatic: In time Shelun swallowed them all.

sentences.zh: 號為強盛，隨水草畜牧。

translations.literal: He became known as powerful and flourishing, following water and pasture with their herds.
translations.idiomatic: His fame as a mighty power spread, and his people followed the grass and water with their herds.

sentences.zh: 其西則焉耆之地，東則朝鮮之地，北則渡沙漠，窮瀚海，南則臨大磧。

translations.literal: To the west lay the lands of Yanqi; to the east the lands of Korea; to the north they crossed the desert to the ends of the Han Sea; to the south they bordered the great sands.
translations.idiomatic: Westward lay the territory of Yanqi; eastward the lands of Korea; northward they crossed the desert to the far edge of the Han Sea; southward they pressed upon the great sands.

sentences.zh: 其常所會庭，敦煌、張掖之北。

translations.literal: Their customary assembly ground lay north of Dunhuang and Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Their usual gathering place for the royal court lay north of Dunhuang and Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 小國皆苦其寇抄，羈縻附之。

translations.literal: Small states all suffered from their raiding and submitted in tributary attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser states groaned under their raids and submitted in tributary dependence.

sentences.zh: 於是自號豆代可汗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he styled himself Khaghan of the Dou Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he proclaimed himself Khaghan of the Dou line.

sentences.zh: 豆代，猶魏言駕馭開張也；

translations.literal: Dou, in Wei speech, means "to drive and open wide";
translations.idiomatic: Dou, in the Wei tongue, means "to drive forth and open wide";

sentences.zh: 可汗，猶魏言皇帝也。

translations.literal: khaghan, in Wei speech, means "emperor."
translations.idiomatic: khaghan, in the Wei tongue, means "emperor."

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕之俗，君及大臣因其行能，即為稱號，若中國立諡。

translations.literal: Among Rouran customs, the ruler and great ministers receive titles based on their conduct and abilities, like posthumous epithets in China.
translations.idiomatic: By Rouran custom the ruler and his great ministers take titles from their deeds and talents, much as China bestows posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 既死之後，不復追稱。

translations.literal: After death they were not given posthumous honors again.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were dead, no further titles were added.

sentences.zh: 道武謂尚書崔宏曰：「蠕蠕之人，昔來號為頑囂，每來抄掠，駕牸牛奔遁，驅犍牛隨之，牸牛伏不能前。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu said to Minister of State Cui Hong: "The Rouran people were formerly called obstinate and arrogant; each time they came raiding they drove calf cows to flee, herding bullocks behind them—the calf cows would lie down unable to go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu told Minister of State Cui Hong: "The Rouran were always called stubborn and overbearing. Whenever they raided they put the heifer-cows in front to run, with bullocks driven behind—the heifers would lie down and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 異部人有教其以犍牛易之來者，蠕蠕曰：'其母尚不能行，而況其子！'

translations.literal: Someone from another tribe taught them to exchange calf cows for steers when coming; the Rouran said, 'If the mother cannot walk, how much less the son!'
translations.idiomatic: A man from another tribe advised them to swap the heifers for steers on the way in. The Rouran replied, 'If the mother cannot walk, how can the son!'

sentences.zh: 終於不易，遂為敵所虜。

translations.literal: In the end they would not exchange them, and were finally captured by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They would not make the exchange, and in the end were taken by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今社侖學中國，立法，置戰陣，卒成邊害。

translations.literal: Now Shelun has learned from China, established laws, and set battle arrays—he has at last become a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shelun has studied the Middle Kingdom, made laws, and arrayed his troops for battle—at last he has become a scourge on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 道家言'聖人生，大盜起'，信矣。」

translations.literal: The Daoists say, 'When a sage is born, great robbers arise'—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: The Daoists say, 'When the sage appears, the great robber is born'—how true that is!"

sentences.zh: 天興五年，社侖聞道武征姚興，遂犯塞，入自參合陂，南至豺山及善無北澤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Shelun heard that Daowu was campaigning against Yao Xing and invaded the frontier, entering from Canhepi, south to Chaoshan and the northern marshes of Shanyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Shelun learned that Daowu was marching against Yao Xing and breached the border, entering by Canhepi and pushing south to Chaoshan and the northern marshes of Shanyou.

sentences.zh: 時遣常山王遵以萬騎追之，不及。

translations.literal: At the time [the court] sent Prince of Changshan Zun with ten thousand cavalry in pursuit, but they could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent the Prince of Changshan, Zun, with ten thousand horse in pursuit, but he could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 天賜中，社侖從弟悅代、大那等謀殺社侖而立大那。

translations.literal: During the reign era of Tianci, Shelun's cousins Yuedai and Dana plotted to kill Shelun and install Dana.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianci era Shelun's cousins Yuedai and Dana plotted to assassinate Shelun and set Dana on the throne.

sentences.zh: 發覺，大那等來奔，以大那為冠軍將軍、西平侯，悅代為越騎校尉、易陽子。

translations.literal: The plot was discovered; Dana and others came to surrender; Dana was made General of the Van and Marquis of Xiping, Yuedai made Colonel of the Skilled Cavalry and Baron of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was uncovered; Dana and his fellows fled to Wei. Dana was appointed General of the Van and Marquis of Xiping; Yuedai was made Colonel of the Skilled Cavalry and Baron of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，社侖寇邊。

translations.literal: In the third summer of [Tianci], Shelun raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the third summer of that era Shelun raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 永興元年冬，又犯塞。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yongxing, he again violated the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Yongxing he again broke into the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 二年，明元討之，社侖遁走，道死。

translations.literal: In the second year, Emperor Mingyuan campaigned against him; Shelun fled and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Emperor Mingyuan took the field against him; Shelun fled and died on the march.

sentences.zh: 其子度拔年少，未能禦眾，部落立社侖弟斛律，號藹苦蓋可汗，魏言姿質美好也。

translations.literal: His son Dubo was young and unable to command the masses; the tribes installed Shelun's younger brother Hulü, styled Khaghan Aikugai—in Wei speech, "of fine appearance."
translations.idiomatic: His son Dubo was still a boy and could not hold the tribe together; the clans raised Shelun's younger brother Hulü and styled him Khaghan Aikugai—"of lovely bearing," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 斛律北並賀術也骨國，東破譬曆辰部落。

translations.literal: Hulü annexed the Heshuyebo state to the north and crushed the Pilichen tribes to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü absorbed the Heshuyebo state in the north and overthrew the Pilichen tribes in the east.

sentences.zh: 三年，斛律宗人悅侯咄牴幹等百數十人來降。

translations.literal: In the third year, more than a hundred of Hulü's clansmen including Yuehoudu and Digan came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year more than a hundred of Hulü's kinsmen, including Yuehoudu and Digan, came over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 斛律畏威自守，不敢南侵，北邊安靜。

translations.literal: Hulü, awed by [Wei's] might, kept to himself and did not dare invade south; the northern frontier was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Awed by Wei's power, Hulü held his own and did not dare strike south; the northern marches were quiet.

sentences.zh: 神瑞元年，與馮跋和媵親，跋娉斛律女為妻，將為交婚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenrui, he concluded a marriage alliance with Feng Ba; Ba took Hulü's daughter as wife and they were to exchange brides.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenrui he made a marriage pact with Feng Ba, who took Hulü's daughter as wife and prepared a reciprocal bridal exchange.

sentences.zh: 斛律長兄子步鹿真謂斛律曰：「女小遠適，憂思生疾，可遣大臣樹黎、勿地延等女為媵。」

translations.literal: Hulü's eldest brother's son Buluzhen said to Hulü: "The girl is young and going far to marry—homesickness will bring illness; you could send the ministers Shuli, Budiyan, and others' daughters as accompanying brides."
translations.idiomatic: Hulü's elder brother's son Buluzhen said to him: "The girl is young and the journey far—longing will make her ill. You could send your ministers Shuli and Budiyan and the others to give their daughters as secondary wives."

sentences.zh: 斛律不許。

translations.literal: Hulü did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü refused.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真出，謂樹黎等曰：「斛律欲令汝女為媵，遠至他國。」

translations.literal: After Buluzhen left, he told Shuli and the others: "Hulü wants to make your daughters accompanying brides and send them far to another country."
translations.idiomatic: When Buluzhen went out he told Shuli and the rest: "Hulü means to make your daughters secondary wives and send them off to a foreign land."

sentences.zh: 黎遂共結謀，令勇士夜就斛律穹廬後，伺其出執之，與女俱嬪于和龍。

translations.literal: Shuli and the others therefore plotted together, sending braves by night to wait behind Hulü's yurt; when he came out they seized him and, with the girl, sent them as brides to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Shuli and his fellows then conspired: at night they posted warriors behind Hulü's yurt, seized him when he came out, and together with the girl sent them as brides to Helong.

sentences.zh: 乃立步鹿真。

translations.literal: Thereupon they installed Buluzhen.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon set up Buluzhen as ruler.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真立，委政樹黎。

translations.literal: Once Buluzhen was established, he entrusted government to Shuli.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen, once enthroned, handed affairs of state to Shuli.

sentences.zh: 初，高車叱洛侯者，叛其渠帥，導社侖破諸部落，社侖德之，以為大人。

translations.literal: Previously there was a Gaoche man Chiluohou who rebelled against his chieftain and guided Shelun in crushing the various tribes; Shelun was grateful and made him a great chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been a Gaoche man named Chiluohou who rebelled against his chieftain and led Shelun to break the other tribes; Shelun was grateful and made him a great chief.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真與社侖子社拔共至叱洛侯家，淫其少妻。

translations.literal: Buluzhen went with Shelun's son Sheba to Chiluohou's house and violated his young wife.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen went with Shelun's son Sheba to Chiluohou's home and violated his young wife.

sentences.zh: 少妻告步鹿真，叱洛侯欲舉大檀為主，遺大檀金馬勒為信。

translations.literal: The young wife told Buluzhen that Chiluohou intended to make Datan ruler, sending Datan a golden horse-bridle as proof.
translations.idiomatic: The young wife told Buluzhen that Chiluohou meant to raise Datan as lord and had sent Datan a golden horse-bridle as token.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真聞之，歸發八千騎往圍，叱洛侯焚其珍寶，自刎而死。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Buluzhen returned and dispatched eight thousand cavalry to surround him; Chiluohou burned his treasures and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen heard this, turned back, and sent eight thousand horse to surround him; Chiluohou burned his valuables and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真遂掩大檀。

translations.literal: Buluzhen then attacked Datan.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen then moved against Datan.

sentences.zh: 大檀發軍執步鹿真及社拔，絞殺之，乃自立。

translations.literal: Datan raised troops, seized Buluzhen and Sheba, strangled them, and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Datan mobilized his forces, seized Buluzhen and Sheba, strangled them, and took the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 大檀者，社侖季父僕渾之子，先統別部鎮於西界，能得眾心，國人推戴之，號牟汗紇升蓋可汗，魏言制勝也。

translations.literal: Datan was the son of Shelun's younger father's younger brother Puhun; he had earlier commanded a separate tribe garrisoning the western marches, won the people's hearts, and the countrymen elevated him, styling him Khaghan Mohankesheng—in Wei speech, "victorious."
translations.idiomatic: Datan was the son of Shelun's uncle Puhun; he had long commanded a separate division on the western frontier, won the people's hearts, and the nation raised him up, styling him Khaghan Mohankesheng—"the conqueror," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 斛律父子既至和龍，馮跋封為上谷侯。

translations.literal: After Hulü and his son arrived at Helong, Feng Ba enfeoffed them as Marquis of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hulü and his son reached Helong, Feng Ba enfeoffed them as Marquises of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 大檀率眾南徙犯塞，明元親討之，大檀懼而遁走。

translations.literal: Datan led his masses south to invade the frontier; Emperor Mingyuan personally campaigned against him, and Datan fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Datan led his people south to raid the border; Emperor Mingyuan took the field in person, and Datan fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 遣山陽侯奚斤等追之，遇寒雪，士眾凍死及墮指者十二三。

translations.literal: [The emperor] sent Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin and others in pursuit; they encountered cold and snow, and of the soldiers two or three tenths froze to death or lost fingers to frostbite.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Marquis of Shanyang, Xi Jin, and others in pursuit; they met bitter cold and snow, and two or three soldiers in ten froze to death or lost fingers to frostbite.

sentences.zh: 及明元崩，太武即位，大檀聞而大喜，始光元年秋，乃寇雲中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan died and Emperor Taiwu succeeded, Datan rejoiced greatly; in the autumn of the first year of Shiguang he raided Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan died and Emperor Taiwu ascended the throne, Datan was overjoyed; in the autumn of the first year of Shiguang he raided Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 太武親討之，三日二夜至雲中。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu personally campaigned against him; in three days and two nights he reached Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu marched against him in person and reached Yunzhong in three days and two nights.

sentences.zh: 大檀騎圍太武五十餘重，騎逼，馬首相次如堵焉。

translations.literal: Datan's cavalry surrounded Taiwu more than fifty ranks deep; the horsemen pressed so close that horse heads formed a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Datan's horsemen ringed Taiwu more than fifty deep; the press was so tight that horse heads stood flank to flank like a wall.

sentences.zh: 士卒大懼。

translations.literal: The soldiers were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 太武顏色自若，眾情乃安。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu's face remained calm, and the army's spirits were steadied.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu's countenance never changed, and the army's hearts grew calm.

sentences.zh: 先是，大檀弟大那與社侖爭國，敗而來奔。

translations.literal: Previously, Datan's younger brother Dana had contested the realm with Shelun, been defeated, and come to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Datan's younger brother Dana had fought Shelun for the realm, been beaten, and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 大檀以大那子於陟斤為部帥。

translations.literal: Datan had made Dana's son Yuzhijin a tribal chief.
translations.idiomatic: Datan had installed Dana's son Yuzhijin as a tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 軍士射于陟斤殺之，大檀恐，乃還。

translations.literal: A soldier's arrow struck and killed Yuzhijin; Datan was terrified and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier's arrow struck Yuzhijin and killed him; Datan was terrified and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 二年，太武大舉征之，東西五道並進。

translations.literal: In the second year, Taiwu mounted a great campaign against him, advancing in five columns from east and west.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Taiwu launched a great expedition, five armies advancing together from east and west.

sentences.zh: 平陽王長孫翰等從黑漠；

translations.literal: Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others [went] from the Black Desert;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingyang, Changsun Han, and others marched from the Black Desert;

sentences.zh: 汝陰公長孫道生從白黑兩漠間；

translations.literal: Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng from between the white and black deserts;
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Ruyin, Changsun Daosheng, from between the white and black deserts;

sentences.zh: 車駕從中道；

translations.literal: the imperial carriage from the central route;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial carriage by the central road;

sentences.zh: 東平公娥清次西，從栗園；

translations.literal: Duke of the Eastern March E Qing second on the west, from Liyuan;
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of the Eastern March, E Qing, on the western wing, from Liyuan;

sentences.zh: 宜城王奚斤、將軍安原等西道，從爾寒山。

translations.literal: Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin and General Anyuan and others on the western route marched from Erhanshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the western route the Prince of Yicheng, Xi Jin, General Anyuan, and others advanced from Erhanshan.

sentences.zh: 諸軍至漠南，舍輜重，輕騎齎十五日糧，絕漠討之。

translations.literal: The armies reached south of the desert, left their baggage, and with light cavalry carried fifteen days' grain, crossed the desert to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies reached the southern desert they cast off their baggage train, took light horse with fifteen days' rations, crossed the wastes, and struck.

sentences.zh: 大檀部落駭驚，北走。

translations.literal: Datan's tribes were terrified and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Datan's people were seized with terror and fled northward.

sentences.zh: 神蒨元年八月，大檀遣子將騎萬餘入塞，殺掠邊人而走，附國高車追擊破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Shenqi, Datan sent his son with more than ten thousand horse to invade the frontier, killing and plundering border people before withdrawing; the affiliated Gaoche tribes pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Shenqi, Datan sent his son at the head of more than ten thousand horsemen into the borderlands to kill and plunder; on the retreat the subject Gaoche tribes overtook and broke them.

sentences.zh: 自廣寧還，追之不及。

translations.literal: Returning from Guangning, [Wei forces] pursued but could not catch them.
translations.idiomatic: As they returned from Guangning the pursuers could not overtake them.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，太武練兵於南郊，將襲大檀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, Taiwu drilled troops at the southern suburb, intending to strike Datan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Taiwu reviewed troops at the southern suburb, preparing to fall upon Datan.

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣皆不願，術士張深、徐辯以天文說止帝，帝從崔浩計而行。

translations.literal: The high ministers all opposed it; the diviners Zhang Shen and Xu Bian used celestial signs to dissuade the emperor, but the emperor followed Cui Hao's plan and marched.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were all against the campaign; the diviners Zhang Shen and Xu Bian argued from the stars that he should not go, yet the emperor took Cui Hao's counsel and set out.

sentences.zh: 會江南使還，稱宋文欲犯河南，謂行人曰：「汝疾還告魏主，歸我河南地，即當罷兵；

translations.literal: When envoys from the south returned, they reported that Emperor Wen of Song meant to invade the Henan region, telling the travelers: "Hurry back and tell the Wei ruler: return our Henan lands and we will cease arms;
translations.idiomatic: Envoys returning from the south reported that Emperor Wen of Song intended to attack the Henan region and told the travelers, "Go quickly and tell the Wei ruler: give back our lands south of the Yellow River and we will lay down arms;

sentences.zh: 不然，盡我將士之力。」

translations.literal: otherwise we will exert all our generals' and soldiers' strength."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise we will bring the full force of our army against you."

sentences.zh: 帝聞而大笑，告公卿曰：「龜鱉小豎，自救不暇，何能為也？

translations.literal: Hearing this the emperor laughed greatly and told the ministers: "That turtle-and-snake whelp can barely save himself—what can he do?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud and told his ministers, "That turtle-and-snake whelp can hardly keep himself alive—what harm can he do?

sentences.zh: 就使能來，若不先滅蠕蠕，便是坐待寇至，腹背受敵，非上策也。

translations.literal: Even if he could come, unless we first destroy the Rouran we would simply sit waiting for the enemy to arrive, caught front and rear—that is no superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he did come, unless we first crush the Rouran we would only sit and let the foe strike us from both sides—that is no sound plan.

sentences.zh: 吾行決矣！」

translations.literal: My mind is made up!"
translations.idiomatic: My decision stands!"

sentences.zh: 於是車駕出東道，向黑山；

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial carriage took the eastern route toward Heishan;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the imperial carriage took the eastern road toward Black Mountain;

sentences.zh: 平陽王長孫翰從西道，向大娥山。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han took the western route toward Da'eshan.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Pingyang, Changsun Han, the western road toward Great Goose Mountain.

sentences.zh: 同會賊庭。

translations.literal: They were to meet at the enemy's court.
translations.idiomatic: The two wings were to unite at the enemy's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 五月，次於沙漠南，舍輜重輕襲之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they halted south of the desert, left baggage, and made a light strike.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they halted south of the desert, shed their heavy train, and struck in force.

sentences.zh: 至栗水，大檀眾西奔。

translations.literal: Reaching the Li River, Datan's masses fled west.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Li River, Datan's host fled westward.

sentences.zh: 弟匹黎先典東落，將赴大檀，遇翰軍，翰縱騎擊之，殺其大人數百。

translations.literal: His younger brother Pili, who had earlier governed the eastern tribes, was going to join Datan but met Han's army; Han loosed his horsemen and struck, killing several hundred of their great chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Pili, who had governed the eastern tribes, was marching to join Datan when he met Han's army; Han charged and killed several hundred of their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 大檀聞之震怖，將其族黨，焚燒廬舍，絕跡西走，莫知所至。

translations.literal: Datan, hearing this, was shaken with fear; he led his clansmen, burned their dwellings, and vanished westward—no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: Datan, hearing this, was stricken with terror; he gathered his kin, burned their camps, and vanished westward—none knew whither.

sentences.zh: 於是國落四散，竄伏山谷，畜產布野，無人收視。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribes scattered in all directions, hiding in valleys; livestock covered the plains with no one to tend them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes scattered into the hills; herds lay across the plains with no hand to gather them.

sentences.zh: 太武緣栗水西行，過漢將竇憲故壘。

translations.literal: Taiwu followed the Li River west, passing the old encampment of the Han general Dou Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu marched west along the Li River, passing the old fortress of the Han general Dou Xian.

sentences.zh: 六月，車駕次於菟園水，去平城三千七百餘里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the imperial carriage halted at Tuyuan River, more than 3,700 li from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the court halted at Tuyuan River, more than three thousand seven hundred li from Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 分軍搜討，東至瀚海，西接張掖水，北度燕然山，東西五千餘里，南北三千里。

translations.literal: Dividing the army to search and subdue, east to the Han Sea, west to the Zhangye River, north across Mount Yanran—more than 5,000 li east to west and 3,000 li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The army was split to hunt them down: east to the Han Sea, west to the Zhangye River, north over Mount Yanran—five thousand li from east to west and three thousand from north to south.

sentences.zh: 高車諸部殺大檀種類前後歸降三十餘萬，俘獲首虜及戎馬百餘萬匹。

translations.literal: The Gaoche tribes killed Datan's kin; before and after, more than 300,000 submitted; captives, heads, and war horses numbered more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche tribes slew Datan's kin; in all more than three hundred thousand came over, and captives, heads, and horses exceeded a million.

sentences.zh: 八月，太武聞東部高車屯巳尼陂，人畜甚眾，去官軍千餘里，遂遣左僕射安原等往討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Taiwu heard that eastern Gaoche were encamped at Sini Marsh with vast herds and people, more than a thousand li from the main army; he sent Left Vice Director Anyuan and others to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Taiwu learned that eastern Gaoche were camped at Sini Marsh with immense herds, a thousand li from the main force; he sent the Left Vice Director Anyuan against them.

sentences.zh: 暨巳尼陂，高車諸部望軍降者數十萬。

translations.literal: When they reached Sini Marsh, several hundred thousand of the Gaoche tribes saw the army and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Sini Marsh several hundred thousand Gaoche clans came out to surrender at sight of the army.

sentences.zh: 大檀部落衰弱，因發疾而死。

translations.literal: Datan's tribe was enfeebled; he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Datan's tribe was broken; he sickened and died.

sentences.zh: 子吳提立，號敕連可汗，魏言神聖也。

translations.literal: His son Wuti succeeded, styled Khaghan Chile—in Wei speech, "divine and holy."
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuti took the throne, styled Khaghan Chile—"sacred," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，北鄙候騎獲吳提南偏邏者二十餘人，太武賜之衣服，遣歸。

translations.literal: Previously, northern frontier scouts had captured more than twenty of Wuti's southern patrols; Taiwu gave them clothing and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier northern scouts had taken more than twenty of Wuti's southern patrols; Taiwu clothed them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 吳提上下感德，故朝貢焉。

translations.literal: High and low in Wuti's realm were moved by this kindness, and therefore they came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti's court, high and low, were moved by this grace, and so they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝厚賓其使而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor richly rewarded the envoys and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lavished gifts on the envoys and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 延和三年二月，以吳提尚西海公主，又遣使者納吳提妹為夫人，又進為左昭儀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Yanhe, Wuti married Princess Xihai, and [Wei] again sent envoys to take Wuti's younger sister as consort, later promoting her to Left Senior Concubine.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yanhe year three Wuti wed Princess Xihai; Wei also took his younger sister as consort and later raised her to Left Senior Concubine.

sentences.zh: 吳提遣其兄禿鹿傀及左右數百人來朝，獻馬二千匹。

translations.literal: Wuti sent his elder brother Tulugui and several hundred attendants to court, presenting two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti sent his elder brother Tulugui and several hundred followers to court with two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，班賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and heaped rewards upon them.

sentences.zh: 至太延二年，乃絕和犯塞，四年，車駕幸五原，遂征之。

translations.literal: By the second year of Taiyan he broke the alliance and violated the frontier; in the fourth year the imperial carriage visited Wuyuan and campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Taiyan he broke peace and raided the border; in the fourth year the emperor went to Wuyuan and took the field against him.

sentences.zh: 樂平王丕、河東公賀多羅督十五將出東道，永昌王健、宜都王穆壽督十五將出西道，車駕出中道。

translations.literal: Prince of Leping Pi and Duke of Hedong Heduo'luo commanded fifteen generals on the eastern route; Prince of Yongchang Jian and Prince of Yidu Mushou commanded fifteen generals on the western route; the imperial carriage took the central route.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Leping, Pi, and the Duke of Hedong, Heduo'luo, led fifteen generals on the east; the Prince of Yongchang, Jian, and the Prince of Yidu, Mushou, fifteen on the west; the emperor marched in the center.

sentences.zh: 至浚稽山，分中道復為二道，陳留王崇從大澤向涿邪山，車駕從浚稽北向天山。

translations.literal: Reaching Junji Mountain, the central route split in two: Prince of Chenliu Chong went from the great marsh toward Zhuoyeshan; the imperial carriage from Junji north toward Heavenly Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Junji Mountain the center divided: the Prince of Chenliu, Chong, struck from the great marsh toward Zhuoyeshan; the emperor from Junji north toward Heavenly Mountain.

sentences.zh: 西登子阜，刻石記行，不見蠕蠕而還。

translations.literal: Westward they ascended Zifu and carved stone to record the march, then returned without finding the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: They climbed Zifu in the west, carved a stone record of the campaign, found no Rouran, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 時漠北大旱，無水草，軍馬多死。

translations.literal: At that time the northern desert suffered great drought with no water or grass; many army horses died.
translations.idiomatic: The northern desert was gripped by drought; grass and water failed and countless horses perished.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕西伐沮渠牧犍，宜都王穆壽輔景穆居守，長樂王嵇敬、建甯王崇二萬人鎮漠南，以備蠕蠕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the imperial carriage campaigned west against Juqu Mujian; Prince of Yidu Mushou assisted Jingmu in holding the capital; Prince of Changle Jijing and Prince of Jianning Chong with twenty thousand men garrisoned south of the desert against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor marched west against Juqu Mujian; the Prince of Yidu, Mushou, stayed to assist Jingmu; the Prince of Changle, Jijing, and the Prince of Jianning, Chong, with twenty thousand men guarded the southern desert against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 吳提果犯塞。

translations.literal: Wuti did indeed violate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti duly struck the border.

sentences.zh: 壽素不設備，賊至七介山，京邑大駭，爭奔中城。

translations.literal: Mushou had made no preparations; when the enemy reached Qijie Mountain the capital was thrown into panic and people rushed into the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Mushou was unprepared; when the raiders reached Qijie Mountain the capital panicked and crowds fled into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 司空長孫道生拒之於吐頹山。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng met them at Tuxian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works, Changsun Daosheng, met them at Tuxian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 吳提之寇也，留其兄乞列歸與北鎮諸軍相守，敬、崇等破乞列歸於陰山之北，獲乞列歸。

translations.literal: In Wuti's raid he left his elder brother Qieliegui to hold the northern garrisons; Jijing, Chong, and others defeated Qieliegui north of Yinshan and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti left his elder brother Qieliegui to face the northern garrisons; Jijing and Chong broke him north of Yinshan and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「沮渠陷我也！」

translations.literal: He sighed: "Juqu has ruined me!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Juqu has undone me!"

sentences.zh: 獲其伯父他吾無鹿胡及其將帥五百人，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: They also captured his uncle Tawuwulu and more than five hundred commanders, beheading more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his uncle Tawuwulu and more than five hundred officers and beheaded over ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 吳提聞而遁走，道生追之，至於漠南而還。

translations.literal: Wuti, hearing this, fled; Daosheng pursued to south of the desert and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti fled on the news; Daosheng pursued to the southern desert and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 真君四年，車駕幸漠南，分軍為四道：樂安王范、建甯王崇各統十五將出東道，樂平王丕督十五將出西道，車駕出中道，中山王辰領十五將為中軍後繼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenjun the imperial carriage visited the southern desert and divided the army into four routes: Prince of Le'an Fan and Prince of Jianning Chong each commanded fifteen generals on the east; Prince of Leping Pi commanded fifteen generals on the west; the imperial carriage took the center; Prince of Zhongshan Chen led fifteen generals as rear guard of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenjun the emperor came to the southern desert and split into four columns: the Princes of Le'an and Jianning, fifteen generals each on the east; the Prince of Leping, Pi, fifteen on the west; the emperor in the center; the Prince of Zhongshan, Chen, with fifteen generals as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 車賀至鹿渾穀，與賊相遇。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Luhun Valley and encountered the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached Luhun Valley and met the foe.

sentences.zh: 吳提遁走，追至頞根河擊破之。

translations.literal: Wuti fled; pursued to the Egen River they routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti fled; pursued to the Egen River they shattered his force.

sentences.zh: 車駕至石水而還。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Shishui and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to Shishui and turned back.

sentences.zh: 五年，復幸漠南，欲襲吳提，吳提遠遁，乃止。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again visited the southern desert intending to strike Wuti; Wuti fled far away and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again came south intending to strike Wuti; Wuti fled beyond reach and the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 吳提死，子吐賀真立，號處可汗，魏言唯也。

translations.literal: When Wuti died, his son Tuhezhen succeeded, styled Khaghan Chu—in Wei speech, "only."
translations.idiomatic: When Wuti died his son Tuhezhen succeeded, styled Khaghan Chu—"the sole one," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，車賀北伐，高涼王那出東道，略陽王羯兒出西道，車駕與景穆自中道出涿邪山。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year the imperial carriage campaigned north; Prince of Gaoliang Na took the eastern route, Prince of Liaoyang Jie'er the western route, and the emperor with Jingmu took the center from Zhuoyeshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year the emperor marched north: the Prince of Gaoliang, Na, on the east; the Prince of Liaoyang, Jie'er, on the west; the emperor and Jingmu in the center from Zhuoyeshan.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真別部帥爾綿他拔等率千餘家來降。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen's subordinate chief Ermiantuoba and others led more than a thousand households to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen's subordinate chief Ermiantuoba and others brought more than a thousand households to submit.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍行數千里，吐賀真新立，恐懼遠遁。

translations.literal: At that time the army had marched several thousand li; Tuhezhen had newly succeeded and, in fear, fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The army had already marched thousands of li; Tuhezhen, newly enthroned, fled in terror to the far north.

sentences.zh: 九月，車駕北伐，高涼王出東道，略陽王羯兒出中道，與諸軍期會于地弗池。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the imperial carriage campaigned north; the Prince of Gaoliang took the eastern route, the Prince of Liaoyang Jie'er the central route, and the armies were to meet at Difu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor marched north again: the Prince of Gaoliang on the east, the Prince of Liaoyang Jie'er in the center, all to unite at Difu Pool.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真悉國精銳，軍資甚盛，圍那數十重。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen mustered the nation's elite with abundant supplies; he surrounded Na dozens of ranks deep.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen gathered the nation's best troops with rich stores and ringed Na's camp dozens of deep.

sentences.zh: 那掘長圍堅守，相持數日。

translations.literal: Na dug a long encirclement and held firm for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Na dug in behind a deep rampart and held for several days.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真數挑戰輒不利，以那眾少而固，疑大軍將至，解圍夜遁。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen challenged battle repeatedly without success; seeing Na's few but solid troops, he suspected the main army was near and lifted the siege by night.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen offered battle again and again without gain; finding Na few but stubborn, he feared the main host was near and broke camp by night.

sentences.zh: 那引軍追之，九日九夜，吐賀真益懼，棄輜重，逾穹隆嶺遠遁。

translations.literal: Na pursued for nine days and nine nights; Tuhezhen grew more afraid, abandoned baggage, crossed Qionglong Ridge, and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Na pursued nine days and nine nights; Tuhezhen, ever more afraid, cast off his baggage, crossed Qionglong Ridge, and fled into the distance.

sentences.zh: 那收其輜重，引軍還，與車駕會於廣澤。

translations.literal: Na gathered the abandoned baggage and withdrew, meeting the imperial carriage at Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Na gathered the abandoned stores and withdrew to meet the emperor at Guangze.

sentences.zh: 略陽王羯兒盡收其人戶、畜產百餘萬。

translations.literal: Prince of Liaoyang Jie'er took all their households and livestock—more than a million head.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liaoyang, Jie'er, seized all their households and herds—more than a million head.

sentences.zh: 自是，吐賀真遂單弱，遠竄，邊疆息警矣。

translations.literal: From this Tuhezhen was left isolated and weak, fleeing far away, and the frontier knew peace.
translations.idiomatic: After this Tuhezhen was broken and alone, driven far off, and the borderlands were quiet.

sentences.zh: 太安四年，車駕北征，騎十萬，車十五萬兩，旌旗千里，遂渡大漠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tai'an the imperial carriage campaigned north with 100,000 horse and 150,000 carts; banners stretched a thousand li as they crossed the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tai'an the emperor marched north with a hundred thousand horse and a hundred fifty thousand carts; banners filled the horizon for a thousand li as they crossed the desert.

sentences.zh: 吐賀真遠遁，其莫弗烏硃駕頹率眾數千落來降，乃刊石記功而還。

translations.literal: Tuhezhen fled far away; his minister Wuzhu Jiatai led several thousand tribes to surrender; they carved stone to record the achievement and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhezhen fled beyond reach; his minister Wuzhu Jiatai led several thousand tribes to submit; they carved stone to commemorate the victory and returned.

sentences.zh: 太武征伐之後，意存休息；

translations.literal: After Taiwu's campaigns he wished to rest;
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwu's wars he sought repose;

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕亦怖威北竄，不敢復南。

translations.literal: the Rouran too were cowed by his might and fled north, not daring to come south again.
translations.idiomatic: the Rouran too were cowed by his might, fled north, and dared not raid south again.

sentences.zh: 和平五年，吐賀真死，子予成立，號受羅部真可汗，魏言惠也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Heping Tuhezhen died; his son Yucheng succeeded, styled Khaghan Shouluobuzhen—in Wei speech, "benevolent."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Heping Tuhezhen died; his son Yucheng succeeded, styled Khaghan Shouluobuzhen—"the gracious," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 自稱永康元年。

translations.literal: He styled his reign the first year of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the first year of his era Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 率部侵塞，北鎮遊軍大破其眾。

translations.literal: He led his tribes to raid the frontier; northern garrison patrols routed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: He led his tribes against the border; northern patrols crushed his army.

sentences.zh: 皇興四年，予成犯塞，車駕北討，京兆王子推、東陽西元丕督諸軍出西道，任城王雲等督軍出東道，汝陰王賜、濟南公羅烏拔督軍為前鋒，隴西王源賀督諸軍為後繼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangxing Yucheng violated the frontier; the imperial carriage campaigned north; Prince of Jingzhao Zitui and Xiyuan Pi of Dongyang commanded armies on the western route; Prince of Rencheng Yun and others on the eastern route; Prince of Ruyin Ci and Duke of Jinan Luowuba led the van; Prince of Longxi Yuanhe commanded the rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangxing Yucheng raided the border; the emperor marched north: the Prince of Jingzhao, Zitui, and Xiyuan Pi of Dongyang on the west; the Prince of Rencheng, Yun, and others on the east; the Prince of Ruyin, Ci, and the Duke of Jinan, Luowuba, in the van; the Prince of Longxi, Yuanhe, in the rear.

sentences.zh: 諸將會車駕于女水之濱，獻文親誓眾，詔諸將曰：「用兵在奇，不在眾也。

translations.literal: The generals met the imperial carriage on the banks of the Nü River; Emperor Xianwen personally swore the troops and charged the generals: "In war, surprise matters, not numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The generals joined the emperor on the Nü River; Emperor Xianwen personally swore the army and told his commanders, "In war it is cunning, not numbers, that counts.

sentences.zh: 卿等但為朕力戰，方略已在朕心。」

translations.literal: You need only fight fiercely for me—the plan is already in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Fight with all your strength for me; the strategy is already settled in my mind."

sentences.zh: 乃選精兵五千人挑戰，多設奇兵以惑之，虜眾奔潰，逐北三十餘里，斬首五萬級，降者萬餘人，戎馬器械，不可稱計。

translations.literal: He then chose five thousand elite troops to challenge battle, set many ambushes to confuse them; the barbarian masses broke and fled; pursued north more than thirty li, fifty thousand heads were cut, more than ten thousand surrendered; war horses and equipment beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He chose five thousand picked men to offer battle, laid many ambushes to bewilder them; the enemy broke and ran; pursued more than thirty li north they took fifty thousand heads and ten thousand prisoners; horses and gear beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 旬有九日，往返六千餘里。

translations.literal: In nineteen days they went and returned more than 6,000 li.
translations.idiomatic: In nineteen days they marched more than six thousand li out and back.

sentences.zh: 改女水曰武川，遂作《北征頌》，刊石紀功。

translations.literal: The Nü River was renamed Wuchuan; he composed the "Ode of the Northern Expedition" and carved stone to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The Nü River was renamed Wuchuan; he wrote the "Ode of the Northern Expedition" and set up a stone inscription.

sentences.zh: 延興五年，予成求通婚聘，有司以予成數犯邊塞，請絕其使，發兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxing Yucheng sought marriage; the officials, because Yucheng had repeatedly violated the frontier, asked to cut off envoys and send troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yanxing Yucheng asked for a marriage alliance; the officials, citing his repeated border raids, urged that envoys be refused and an army sent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蠕蠕譬若禽獸，貪而亡義，朕要當以信誠待物，不可抑絕也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Rouran are like birds and beasts—greedy and without righteousness; I must treat all things with sincere good faith and cannot simply cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Rouran are like wild beasts—greedy and faithless; yet I must meet all with honest good faith and cannot simply shut them out.

sentences.zh: 予成知悔前非，遣使請和，求結姻援，安可孤其款意？」

translations.literal: Yucheng knows his former errors and sends envoys to seek peace and a marriage tie—how can I reject his earnest wish?"
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng repents his past wrongs and sends envoys to sue for peace and kinship—how can I spurn his sincere plea?"

sentences.zh: 乃詔報曰：「所論婚事，今始一反，尋覽事理，未允厥中。

translations.literal: He thereupon replied by edict: "As for the marriage you propose, this is your first reversal; reading the matter, it does not sit right.
translations.idiomatic: He answered by edict: "Your talk of marriage comes only now, after your turnabout; weighed in fairness, it does not satisfy.

sentences.zh: 夫男而下女，爻象所明，初婚之吉，敦崇禮聘，君子所以重人倫之本。

translations.literal: That the male should be below the female is shown in the hexagrams; the blessing of a first marriage lies in honoring the rites of betrothal—this is how the gentleman esteems the root of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: That the man should stand above the woman is plain in the Book of Changes; a proper first marriage rests on solemn betrothal—the gentleman thereby honors the foundation of human order.

sentences.zh: 不敬其初，令終難矣。」

translations.literal: If the beginning is not respected, a good end will be hard to achieve."
translations.idiomatic: Where the beginning lacks respect, a worthy end is hard to reach."

sentences.zh: 予成懷譎詐，終獻文世，更不求婚。

translations.literal: Yucheng harbored deceit and through Emperor Xianwen's reign never again sought marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng nursed treachery and through Emperor Xianwen's reign never again asked for a bride.

sentences.zh: 太和元年四月，遣莫何去汾比拔等來獻良馬、貂裘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Taihe he sent Moguhui Qinbaba and others to present fine horses and sable furs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Taihe he sent Moguhui Qinbaba and others with fine horses and sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 比拔等稱：「伏承天朝珍寶華麗甚積，求一觀之。」

translations.literal: Qinbaba and the others said: "We have heard that the heavenly court's treasures and splendors are piled high; we beg to see them."
translations.idiomatic: Qinbaba said, "We hear the heavenly court's treasures are heaped in splendor; we beg a glimpse."

sentences.zh: 乃敕有司，出禦府珍玩、金玉、文繡、器物，禦廄文馬、奇禽、異獸及人間所宜用者，列之京肆，令其曆觀焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the authorities to bring out from the imperial store jewels, gold and jade, brocades, utensils, imperial stable horses with patterned coats, rare birds and beasts, and whatever men commonly use, and display them in the capital market for them to view in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the imperial treasury opened—jewels, gold, brocades, vessels, patterned steeds, rare birds and beasts, and everyday luxuries—and arrayed them in the capital market for the envoys to walk through.

sentences.zh: 比拔見之，自相謂曰：「大國富麗，一生所未見也。」

translations.literal: Seeing them, Qinbaba said to one another: "The great state is rich and magnificent—never in our lives have we seen the like."
translations.idiomatic: Qinbaba whispered among themselves, "The great state is rich beyond anything we have ever seen."

sentences.zh: 二年二月，又遣比拔等朝貢，尋復請婚焉。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year they again sent Qinbaba and others with tribute, and soon asked for marriage again.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year two they came again with tribute and once more asked for marriage.

sentences.zh: 孝文志在招納，許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, intent on winning them over, consented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, wishing to win them over, agreed.

sentences.zh: 予成雖歲貢不絕，而款約不著，婚事亦停。

translations.literal: Though Yucheng sent tribute every year without fail, his sincere undertakings were not recorded and the marriage too was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yucheng sent tribute year after year, his pledges rang hollow and the marriage was never concluded.

sentences.zh: 九年，予成死，子豆侖立，號伏古敦可汗，魏言恆也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Yucheng died; his son Doulun succeeded, styled Khaghan Fugudun—in Wei speech, "constant."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Yucheng died; his son Doulun succeeded, styled Khaghan Fugudun—"the enduring," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 自稱太平元年。

translations.literal: He styled his reign the first year of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the first year of his era Taiping.

sentences.zh: 豆侖性殘暴好殺。

translations.literal: Doulun was by nature cruel and fond of killing.
translations.idiomatic: Doulun was cruel by nature and delighted in bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 其名臣侯醫垔、石洛候數以忠言諫之，又勸與魏通和，勿侵中國。

translations.literal: His worthy ministers Houyigai and Shiluohou repeatedly admonished him with loyal words and urged peace with Wei and that he not invade China.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers Houyigai and Shiluohou repeatedly spoke plainly, urging peace with Wei and no raids on the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 豆侖怒，誣石洛候謀反，殺之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Doulun in anger falsely accused Shiluohou of plotting rebellion, killed him, and exterminated his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Doulun in rage accused Shiluohou of treason, slew him, and wiped out three generations of his house.

sentences.zh: 十六年八月，孝文遣陽平王頤、左僕射陸睿並為都督，領軍斛律桓等十二將七萬騎討豆侖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year Emperor Xiaowen sent Prince of Yangping Yi and Left Vice Director Lu Rui as commanders, with General Hulu Huan and twelve other generals and seventy thousand horse to campaign against Doulun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year Emperor Xiaowen sent the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and the Left Vice Director Lu Rui as commanders, with General Hulu Huan and twelve other generals at the head of seventy thousand horse against Doulun.

sentences.zh: 部內高車阿伏至羅率眾十餘萬西走，自立為主。

translations.literal: Within the tribes the Gaoche chief Afozheluo led more than 100,000 westward, set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Within his realm the Gaoche chief Afozheluo led more than a hundred thousand west and proclaimed himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 豆侖與叔父那蓋為二道追之。

translations.literal: Doulun and his uncle Nagai pursued in two columns.
translations.idiomatic: Doulun and his uncle Nagai gave chase in two columns.

sentences.zh: 豆侖出自浚稽山北而西，那蓋出自金山。

translations.literal: Doulun marched out north of Junji Mountain toward the west; Nagai marched out from Golden Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Doulun advanced from north of Junji Mountain westward; Nagai came out from Golden Mountain.

sentences.zh: 豆侖頻為阿伏至羅所敗，那蓋累有勝捷。

translations.literal: Doulun was repeatedly defeated by Afozheluo; Nagai won victory after victory.
translations.idiomatic: Doulun suffered defeat after defeat at Afozheluo's hands; Nagai won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 四人咸以那蓋為天所助，欲推那蓋為主。

translations.literal: All four men said Nagai was aided by Heaven and wished to elevate Nagai as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: All four declared that Heaven favored Nagai and pressed him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 那蓋不從，眾強之。

translations.literal: Nagai would not consent; the masses forced him.
translations.idiomatic: Nagai refused; the people compelled him.

sentences.zh: 那蓋曰：「我為臣不可，焉能為主？」

translations.literal: Nagai said: "As a subject I cannot; how could I become ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: Nagai said, "I am fit to serve, not to rule—how could I be khaghan?"

sentences.zh: 眾乃殺豆侖母子，以屍示那蓋，乃襲位。

translations.literal: The masses then killed Doulun and his mother, displayed the corpses to Nagai, and thereupon he took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then slew Doulun and his mother, showed the bodies to Nagai, and only then did he accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 那蓋號候其伏代庫者可汗，魏言悅樂也。

translations.literal: Nagai styled himself Khaghan Houqifudaiku— in Wei speech, "joyful."
translations.idiomatic: Nagai styled himself Khaghan Houqifudaiku—"delight," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 自稱太安元年。

translations.literal: He styled his reign the first year of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the first year of his era Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 那蓋死，子伏圖立，號他汗可汗，魏言緒也。

translations.literal: When Nagai died, his son Futou succeeded, styled Khaghan Tahan—in Wei speech, "thread" or "beginning."
translations.idiomatic: When Nagai died his son Futou succeeded, styled Khaghan Tahan—"the beginning," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 自稱始平元年。

translations.literal: He styled his reign the first year of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the first year of his era Shiping.

sentences.zh: 正始三年，伏圖遣使紇奚勿六跋朝獻，請求通和。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi, Futou sent the envoy Hexi Wuliubaba with tribute, requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengshi, Futou sent the envoy Hexi Wuliubaba to court with tribute and a plea for peace.

sentences.zh: 宣武不報其使，詔有司敕勿六跋曰：「蠕蠕遠祖社侖是大魏叛臣，往者包容，暫時通使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu did not reply to the envoy but ordered the authorities to instruct Wuliubaba: "Shelun, the Rouran remote ancestor, was a great rebel against Wei; in former days we tolerated them and briefly exchanged envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu gave no answer to the envoy but ordered the officials to tell Wuliubaba, "Your remote forebear Shelun was a traitor to Great Wei; we once indulged you and briefly received your envoys.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕衰微，有損疇日；

translations.literal: Now the Rouran are enfeebled, a shadow of their former days;
translations.idiomatic: Now the Rouran are feeble, a far cry from their former might;

sentences.zh: 大魏之德，方隆周、漢，跨據中原，指清八表。

translations.literal: Great Wei's virtue rises to match Zhou and Han, spanning the central plains and aiming to pacify the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei's virtue now rivals Zhou and Han; we hold the heartland and mean to bring order to the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 正以江南未平，權寬北略。

translations.literal: Only because the south is not yet settled do we temporarily relax the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the south is not yet pacified do we for the moment spare the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 通和之事，未容相許。

translations.literal: Matters of alliance cannot yet be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Peace cannot yet be granted you.

sentences.zh: 若修蕃禮，款誠昭著者，當不孤爾也。」

translations.literal: If you observe tributary rites and your sincerity is clearly shown, we shall not disappoint you."
translations.idiomatic: If you observe proper tributary rites and your good faith is plain, we shall not fail you."

sentences.zh: 永平元年，伏圖又遣勿六跋奉函書一封，並獻貂裘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping, Futou again sent Wuliubaba with a letter in a case and presented sable furs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongping, Futou again sent Wuliubaba with a sealed letter and sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 宣武不納，依前喻遣。

translations.literal: Xuanwu did not accept them and sent them away with the former admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu would not receive them and dismissed them with the same rebuke as before.

sentences.zh: 伏圖西征高車，為高車王彌俄突所殺。

translations.literal: Futou campaigned west against the Gaoche and was killed by the Gaoche king Mie'etuo.
translations.idiomatic: Futou marched west against the Gaoche and was slain by the Gaoche king Mie'etuo.

sentences.zh: 子醜奴立，號豆羅伏拔豆伐可汗，魏言彰制也，自稱建昌元年。

translations.literal: His son Chounu succeeded, styled Khaghan Douluofubadoufa—in Wei speech, "manifest control"—and styled his reign the first year of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chounu succeeded, styled Khaghan Douluofubadoufa—"clear dominion," in the Wei tongue—and proclaimed the first year of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 永平四年九月，醜奴遣沙門洪宣奉獻珠像。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Yongping, Chounu sent the monk Hongxuan to present a jeweled image.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Yongping, Chounu sent the monk Hongxuan with a jeweled Buddha image.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年冬，宣武遣驍騎將軍馬義舒使於醜奴，未發而崩，事遂停寢。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Yanchang, Xuanwu sent Valiant Cavalry General Ma Yishu as envoy to Chounu; before he set out Xuanwu died and the mission was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Yanchang, Xuanwu sent the Valiant Cavalry General Ma Yishu to Chounu; before he departed the emperor died and the mission lapsed.

sentences.zh: 醜奴壯健，善用兵。

translations.literal: Chounu was strong and skilled in the use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu was powerfully built and skilled in war.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣使俟斤尉比建朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he sent the envoy Houjin Weibijian with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent the envoy Houjin Weibijian to court.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年，西征高車大破之，禽其主彌俄突，殺之，盡並叛者，國遂強盛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping he campaigned west against the Gaoche, routed them greatly, captured their king Mie'etuo and killed him, absorbed all the rebels, and the state grew powerful.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiping he marched west, crushed the Gaoche, seized their king Mie'etuo and executed him, absorbed every rebel band, and the realm grew mighty.

sentences.zh: 二年，又遣使俟斤尉比建、紇奚勿六跋、鞏顧禮等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year he again sent envoys Houjin Weibijian, Hexi Wuliubaba, Gongguli, and others with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he again sent Weibijian, Wuliubaba, Gongguli, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年二月，明帝臨顯陽殿，引顧禮等二十人于殿下，遣中書舍人徐紇宣詔，讓以蠕蠕蕃禮不備之意。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Shengui, Emperor Ming held court at Xianyang Hall and summoned Gongguli and twenty others below the steps; he sent Secretariat Attendant Xu He to proclaim an edict reproaching them for incomplete Rouran tributary rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Shengui, Emperor Ming sat at Xianyang Hall and called Gongguli and twenty others before the steps; the Secretariat Attendant Xu He read an edict rebuking their defective tributary observances.

sentences.zh: 初，豆侖之死也，那蓋為主，伏圖納豆侖之妻候呂陵氏，生醜奴、阿那環等六人。

translations.literal: When Doulun died and Nagai became ruler, Futou took Doulun's wife, the Hou Lü clan, who bore Chounu, Anagui, and six sons in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Doulun was killed and Nagai took power, Futou married Doulun's widow of the Hou Lü clan, who bore Chounu, Anagui, and six sons in all.

sentences.zh: 醜奴立後，忽亡一子，字祖惠，求募不能得。

translations.literal: After Chounu succeeded, a son suddenly vanished—named Zuhui—and though they sought and recruited widely he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: After Chounu came to the throne a son vanished—a boy named Zuhui—and though they searched everywhere he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 有屋引副升牟妻是豆渾地萬，年二十許，為醫巫，假託神鬼，先常為醜奴所信，出入去來。

translations.literal: There was a woman of about twenty, wife of Wuyinfusheng Mou, named Douhundiwang, a shaman who feigned communion with spirits; Chounu had long trusted her and she came and went freely.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of about twenty, wife of Wuyinfusheng Mou, named Douhundiwang, passed herself off as a spirit-medium; Chounu had long trusted her and she moved freely in and out of court.

sentences.zh: 乃言：「此兒今在天上，我能呼得。」

translations.literal: She said: "This child is now in Heaven; I can call him back."
translations.idiomatic: She declared, "The boy is in Heaven now; I can summon him back."

sentences.zh: 醜奴母子欣悅。

translations.literal: Chounu and his mother were delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu and his mother rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 後歲仲秋，在大澤中施帳屋，齋潔七日，祈請天神。

translations.literal: Later, in mid-autumn of that year, in the great marsh they pitched a tent, kept pure fast for seven days, and prayed to the heavenly god.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at mid-autumn, they raised a tent in the great marsh, fasted seven days in purity, and prayed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 經一宿，祖惠忽在帳中，自雲恆在天上。

translations.literal: After one night Zuhui suddenly appeared in the tent, saying he had always been in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After one night Zuhui suddenly stood in the tent, claiming he had always been in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 醜奴母子抱之悲喜，大會國人，號地萬為聖女，納為可賀敦。

translations.literal: Chounu and his mother embraced him in joy and sorrow; they convoked the nation, styled Diwang a holy woman, and took her as Khatun.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu and his mother embraced him in tears of joy; the nation was assembled, Diwang was hailed as a holy woman, and she was made Khatun.

sentences.zh: 授夫副升牟爵位，賜牛、馬、羊三千頭。

translations.literal: Her husband Fusheng Mou was given rank and granted three thousand head of cattle, horses, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband Fusheng Mou was ennobled and given three thousand cattle, horses, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 地萬既挾左道，亦是有姿色，醜奴甚加重愛，信用其言，亂其國政。

translations.literal: Diwang, wielding heterodox ways and also comely in appearance, Chounu loved her exceedingly, trusted her words, and she threw the state's government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Diwang practiced sorcery and was besides handsome; Chounu doted on her, believed everything she said, and she threw the government into chaos.

sentences.zh: 如是積歲，祖惠年長，其母問之。

translations.literal: Thus for years; when Zuhui grew older his mother questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed; when Zuhui grew older his mother questioned him.

sentences.zh: 祖惠言：「我恆在地萬家，不嚐上天。

translations.literal: Zuhui said: "I was always at Diwang's house and never went to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zuhui said, "I was always in Diwang's house—I never went to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 上天者，地萬教也。」

translations.literal: Going to Heaven was Diwang's teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was only what Diwang taught me to say."

sentences.zh: 其母具以狀告醜奴。

translations.literal: His mother reported the full circumstances to Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told Chounu the whole story.

sentences.zh: 醜奴言地萬懸鑒遠事，不可不信，勿用讒言也。

translations.literal: Chounu said Diwang's mirror saw far-off things and could not be disbelieved; slander was not to be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu said Diwang's vision reached distant things and must be trusted; he would hear no slander.

sentences.zh: 既而地萬恐懼，譖祖惠於醜奴，醜奴陰殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Diwang in fear slandered Zuhui to Chounu, and Chounu secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Diwang, afraid, denounced Zuhui to Chounu, and Chounu had the boy killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 正光初，醜奴母遣莫何去汾李具列等絞殺地萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang, Chounu's mother sent Moguhui Lijulie and others to strangle Diwang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhengguang, Chounu's mother sent Moguhui Lijulie and others to strangle Diwang.

sentences.zh: 醜奴怒，欲誅具列等。

translations.literal: Chounu was furious and wished to execute Lijulie and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu raged and meant to put Lijulie and his fellows to death.

sentences.zh: 又阿至羅侵醜奴，醜奴擊之，軍敗還，為母與其大臣所殺，立醜奴弟阿那瑰為主。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Azheluo invaded Chounu; Chounu struck him, his army was defeated and he returned; his mother and the great ministers killed him and installed Chounu's younger brother Anagui as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Azheluo attacked Chounu; Chounu met him, was beaten, and on his return his mother and the chief ministers slew him and set up his younger brother Anagui.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰立經十日，其族兄俊力發示發率眾數萬以伐，阿那瑰戰敗，將弟乙居伐輕騎南走歸魏。

translations.literal: Ten days after Anagui's accession his clansman Junlifa Shifa led tens of thousands to attack; Anagui was defeated and fled south to Wei with his younger brother Yijuwa at the head of light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after Anagui took the throne his kinsman Junlifa Shifa marched against him with tens of thousands; beaten, Anagui fled south to Wei with his brother Yijuwa and a light escort.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰母候呂陵氏及其二弟尋為示發所殺，而阿那瑰未之知也。

translations.literal: Anagui's mother the Hou Lü clan and his two younger brothers were soon killed by Shifa, but Anagui did not yet know it.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui's mother of the Hou Lü clan and two younger brothers were soon killed by Shifa, though Anagui did not yet know it.

sentences.zh: 九月，阿那瑰將至，明帝遣兼侍中陸希道為使主，兼散騎常侍孟威為使副，迎勞近畿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, as Anagui was nearing [the border], Emperor Ming sent Concurrent Palace Attendant Lu Xidao as chief envoy and Concurrent Cadet of the Irregular Cavalry Meng Wei as deputy to welcome and comfort him in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, as Anagui drew near, Emperor Ming sent Lu Xidao as chief envoy and Meng Wei as deputy to welcome him in the outer suburbs.

sentences.zh: 使司空公、京兆王繼至北中，侍中崔光、黃門郎元纂在近郊，並申宴勞，引至闕下。

translations.literal: The envoy Minister of Works and Prince of Jingzhao Ji reached Beizhong; Palace Attendant Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Zuan in the near suburbs—all extended banquets and led him to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and Prince of Jingzhao Ji met him at Beizhong; Palace Attendant Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Zuan feasted him in the near suburbs and escorted him to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十月，明帝臨顯陽殿，引從五品已上清官、皇宗、籓國使客等，列於殿庭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Emperor Ming sat at Xianyang Hall and summoned officials of the fifth rank and above in clear posts, imperial clansmen, and envoys from vassal states, arranging them in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor sat at Xianyang Hall and gathered officials of the fifth rank and above, imperial kin, and foreign envoys in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 王公已下及阿那瑰等入就庭中，北面。

translations.literal: Princes and below and Anagui and others entered the courtyard and faced north.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and below, with Anagui and his party, entered the court and faced north.

sentences.zh: 位定，謁者引王公已下升殿，阿那瑰位於籓王之下，又引特命之官及阿那瑰弟並二叔升，位於群官之下。

translations.literal: When places were fixed, the usher led princes and below up the hall; Anagui was placed below the frontier princes, and specially appointed officials together with Anagui's younger brother and two uncles were led up and placed below the mass of officials.
translations.idiomatic: When all were in place, princes and ministers ascended the hall; Anagui stood below the frontier kings; his brother and two uncles were brought up and placed below the other officials.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人曹道宣詔勞問。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Secretariat Attendant Cao Daoxuan to proclaim edicts of inquiry and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Secretariat Attendant Cao Daoxuan to read edicts of greeting and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰啟云：「陛下優隆，命臣弟、叔等升殿預會。

translations.literal: Anagui submitted: "Your Majesty's gracious elevation has allowed my younger brother, uncles, and others to ascend the hall and join this assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui petitioned, "Your Majesty's grace has allowed my brother, uncles, and others to ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 但臣有從兄，在北之日，官高於二叔，乞命升殿。」

translations.literal: But I have a cousin who, while we were in the north, held higher office than my two uncles; I beg that he too be allowed to ascend."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have a cousin who in the north outranked my two uncles; I beg that he too be permitted on the hall."

sentences.zh: 詔聽之，乃位於阿那瑰弟之下，二叔之上。

translations.literal: The edict granted it; he was placed below Anagui's younger brother and above the two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented; he was placed below Anagui's brother and above the two uncles.

sentences.zh: 宴將罷，阿那瑰執所啟立於座後。
