translations.literal: As the banquet was ending, Anagui held his submitted petition standing behind his seat.
translations.idiomatic: As the feast drew to a close, Anagui stood behind his seat holding his written petition.

sentences.zh: 詔遣舍人常景問所欲言。

translations.literal: The edict sent Attendant Chang Jing to ask what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Attendant Chang Jing to ask what he wished to say.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰求詣帝前，詔引之。

translations.literal: Anagui asked to approach the emperor; the edict led him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui asked to approach the throne; he was summoned forward.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰再拜跽曰：「臣先世源由，出於大魏。」

translations.literal: Anagui bowed twice kneeling and said: "My forebears' origin springs from Great Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Anagui knelt, bowed twice, and said, "My ancestors sprang from Great Wei."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕已具知。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "I am already fully informed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know it already."

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰起而言曰：「臣之先，逐草放牧，遂居漠北。」

translations.literal: Anagui rose and said: "My ancestors followed the grass to pasture and so came to dwell in the northern desert."
translations.idiomatic: Anagui rose and said, "My forebears followed the pasturelands and settled in the northern wastes."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿言未盡，可具陳之。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Your words are not complete; you may state them fully."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have not finished; speak fully."

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰又言曰：「臣祖先已來，世居北土，雖復隔越山津，而乃恭心慕化，未能時宣者，正以高車悖逆，臣國擾攘，不暇遣使以宜遠誠。

translations.literal: Anagui again said: "From our ancestors' time we have dwelt in the northern land; though mountains and rivers divided us, our hearts revered transformation; the reason we could not send envoys in season was simply that the Gaoche rebelled and our state was in turmoil, with no leisure to send envoys to declare our distant sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui continued, "Since our ancestors' day we have lived in the north; though mountains and rivers lay between us, our hearts honored your civilization. We could not send envoys in good time only because the Gaoche rebelled and our realm was torn by strife.

sentences.zh: 自頃年已前，漸定高車，及臣兄為主，故遣鞏顧禮等使來大魏，實欲虔修籓禮。

translations.literal: In recent years we have gradually pacified the Gaoche, and when my elder brother became ruler he therefore sent Gongguli and others to Great Wei, truly wishing devoutly to observe tributary rites.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years we subdued the Gaoche, and when my elder brother ruled he sent Gongguli and others to Great Wei, truly wishing to observe full tributary rites.

sentences.zh: 是以曹道芝北使之日，臣與主兄，即遣大臣五人，拜受詔命。

translations.literal: Therefore on the day Cao Daozhi came north as envoy, my elder brother and I at once sent five great ministers to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Daozhi came north as your envoy, my brother and I at once sent five great ministers to receive your edict.

sentences.zh: 臣兄弟本心，未及上徹。

translations.literal: My brother's and my true intent had not yet reached Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: My brother's and my true hearts had not yet reached Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 但高車從而侵暴，中有奸臣，因亂作逆，殺臣兄，立臣為主。

translations.literal: But the Gaoche followed with invasion and violence; among us were traitors who, taking advantage of disorder, rebelled, killed my brother, and set me up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: But the Gaoche invaded; traitors seized the chaos, slew my brother, and set me on the throne.

sentences.zh: 裁過旬日，臣以陛下恩慈如天，是故倉卒輕身投國，歸命陛下。」

translations.literal: Barely ten days passed before I, because Your Majesty's kindness is like Heaven, therefore in haste left my body and came to the state, placing my life in Your Majesty's hands."
translations.idiomatic: Barely ten days later, knowing Your Majesty's kindness is like Heaven, I fled my realm and cast myself on your mercy."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「具卿所陳，理猶未盡，可更言之。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "What you have stated is still not complete; you may speak again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you have said is still incomplete; continue."

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰再拜受詔，起而言曰：「臣以家難，輕來投闕，老母在彼，萬里分張，本國臣人，皆已迸散。

translations.literal: Anagui bowed twice, received the edict, rose and said: "Because of troubles in my house I came lightly to your gates; my old mother remains there, ten thousand li parted from me; the men of my country have all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui bowed, rose, and said, "Family disaster drove me to your gates; my old mother remains there a thousand leagues away; my people have all fled.

sentences.zh: 陛下隆恩，有過天地，求乞兵馬，還向本國，誅翦叛逆，收集亡散。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's lofty grace exceeds Heaven and earth; I beg horses and troops to return to my country, cut down the rebels, and gather the lost and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace exceeds Heaven and earth; I beg horses and troops to return home, destroy the rebels, and gather the scattered.

sentences.zh: 陛下慈念，賜借兵馬，老母若在，得生相見，以申母子之恩；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty in compassion lends me troops and horses, and my old mother still lives, mother and son may meet again and fulfill the bond of parent and child;
translations.idiomatic: If you lend me an army, and my mother still lives, we may meet again and fulfill a son's duty;

sentences.zh: 如其死也，即得報讎，以雪大恥。

translations.literal: if she is dead, I may yet take revenge and wash away this great shame.
translations.idiomatic: if she is dead, I may yet avenge her and wipe away this great shame.

sentences.zh: 臣當統臨餘人，奉事陛下，四時之貢，不敢闕絕。

translations.literal: I shall lead the remnant people in serving Your Majesty; the tribute of the four seasons I dare not neglect.
translations.idiomatic: I shall rule what remains and serve you; the tribute of the four seasons shall not fail.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖顏難睹，敢不披陳？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sacred countenance is hard to behold—how dare I not speak plainly?
translations.idiomatic: Your sacred face is hard for me to behold—how could I not speak plainly?

sentences.zh: 但所欲言者，口不能盡言。

translations.literal: But what I wish to say my mouth cannot fully utter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I would say my tongue cannot fully tell.

sentences.zh: 別有辭啟，謹以仰呈，原垂昭覽。」

translations.literal: I have a separate written petition which I respectfully present; I beg you to look upon it with clear eyes."
translations.idiomatic: I have a written petition which I respectfully offer; I beg your gracious reading."

sentences.zh: 仍以啟付舍人常景，具以奏聞。

translations.literal: He thereupon handed the petition to Attendant Chang Jing, who presented it in full.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the petition to Chang Jing, who laid it before the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋封阿那瑰朔方郡公、蠕蠕王，賜以衣冕，加之軺、蓋，祿從儀衛，同于戚籓。

translations.literal: Soon Anagui was enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang and King of the Rouran, granted robes and regalia, chariot canopy and insignia, salary and guards like a royal kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Anagui was made Duke of Shuofang and King of the Rouran, given robes and regalia, chariot and canopy, guards and stipend like an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 十二月，明帝以阿那瑰國無定主，思還綏集，占請切至，詔議之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, because Anagui's state had no settled ruler and he earnestly wished to return and gather his people, the emperor ordered deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, because his realm lacked a settled ruler and he begged urgently to return and restore his people, the court was ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 時朝臣意有同異，或言聽還，或言不可。

translations.literal: At that time the court ministers were divided—some said let him return, some said he must not.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were divided: some favored sending him back, some opposed it.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉為宰相，阿那瑰私以金百斤貨之，遂歸北。

translations.literal: Chief Commander Yuan Cha was chief minister; Anagui privately bribed him with a hundred catties of gold, and so he was sent north.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Yuan Cha received a hundred catties of gold from Anagui in secret, and the decision went to send him north.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，阿那瑰等五十四人請辭，明帝臨西堂，引見阿那瑰及其叔伯兄弟五人，升階賜坐，遣中書舍人穆弼宣勞。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Anagui and fifty-four others asked leave; Emperor Ming sat at the Western Hall and received Anagui and his uncles and brothers five in number, had them ascend the steps and be seated, and sent Secretariat Attendant Mu Bi to proclaim comfort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Anagui and fifty-four followers took leave; the emperor sat at the Western Hall, received Anagui and five uncles and brothers, seated them on the steps, and sent Mu Bi to speak words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰等拜辭。

translations.literal: Anagui and the others bowed in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui and his party bowed farewell.

sentences.zh: 詔賜阿那瑰細明光人馬鎧一具，鐵人馬鎧六具，露絲銀纏槊二張並白眊，赤漆槊十張並白眊，黑漆槊十張並幡，露絲弓二張並箭，硃漆柘弓六張並箭，黑漆弓十張並箭，赤漆楯幡並刀，黑漆楯六幡並刀，赤漆鼓角二十具，五色錦被二領，黃槹被褥三十具，私府繡袍一領並帽，內者緋納襖一領、緋袍二十領並帽，內者雜彩千段，緋納小口袴褶一具內中宛具，紫納大口袴褶一具內中宛具，百子帳十八具，黃布幕六張，新乾飯一百石，麥<麥少>八石，榛<麥少>五石，銅烏錥四枚、柔鐵烏錥二枚各受二斛。

translations.literal: The edict granted Anagui one set of fine Mingguang horse-and-man armor, six sets of iron horse-and-man armor, two silver-wrapped spears with white veils, ten red-lacquered spears with white veils, ten black-lacquered spears with banners, two bows with arrows, six vermilion-lacquered catalpa bows with arrows, ten black-lacquered bows with arrows, red-lacquered shields with banners and swords, six black-lacquered shields with banners and swords, twenty red-lacquered drums and horns, two brocade quilts of five colors, thirty sets of yellow bedding, one embroidered robe and cap from the privy store, one crimson padded coat and twenty crimson robes with caps for attendants, a thousand lengths of mixed silks for attendants, one set of crimson narrow trousers and jacket with undergarments, one set of purple wide trousers and jacket with undergarments, eighteen hundred-son tents, six yellow cloth awnings, a hundred shi of dried grain, eight shi of wheat bran, five shi of hazelnut bran, four copper wuyu vessels and two soft-iron wuyu vessels each holding two hu.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted him one suit of fine Mingguang armor for man and horse, six suits of iron armor, two silver-bound spears with white veils, ten red-lacquered spears, ten black-lacquered spears with pennants, bows and arrows in quantity, shields, swords, twenty drums and horns, brocade bedding, robes for himself and twenty crimson robes for attendants, a thousand lengths of silk, full wardrobes inner and outer, eighteen tents, grain and fodder by the hundred shi, and bronze and iron cauldrons of two hu each—an inventory of imperial largesse beyond easy counting.

sentences.zh: 黑漆竹榼四枚各受五升，婢二口，父草馬五百疋，駝百二十頭，牸牛一百頭，羊五千口，硃畫盤器十合，粟二十萬石，至鎮給之。

translations.literal: Four black-lacquered bamboo flasks each holding five sheng, two maidservants, five hundred stallions of his father's breed, a hundred twenty camels, a hundred cows, five thousand sheep, ten sets of vermilion-painted vessels, two hundred thousand shi of millet—to be supplied at the frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: Four black bamboo flasks of five sheng, two maidservants, five hundred stallions, a hundred twenty camels, a hundred cows, five thousand sheep, painted vessels, and two hundred thousand shi of millet to be issued at the border garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔侍中崔光、黃門元纂，郭外勞遣。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Palace Attendant Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan to see them off and comfort them outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan were ordered to escort them beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰來奔之後，其從父兄俟力發婆羅門率數萬人入討示發，破之。

translations.literal: After Anagui came to surrender, his cousin's elder brother Houli Faboluomen led tens of thousands to attack Shifa and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Anagui fled to Wei, his cousin's elder brother Houli Faboluomen led tens of thousands against Shifa and broke him.

sentences.zh: 示發走奔地豆幹，為其所殺。

translations.literal: Shifa fled to Didugan and was killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Shifa fled to Didugan and was slain by him.

sentences.zh: 推婆羅門為主，號彌偶可社句可汗，魏言安靜也。

translations.literal: They elevated Faboluomen as ruler, styled Khaghan Mioukesheju—in Wei speech, "tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: They raised Faboluomen as ruler, styled Khaghan Mioukesheju—"the peaceful," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 時安北將軍、懷朔鎮將楊鈞表：「傳聞彼人已立主，是阿那瑰同堂兄弟。

translations.literal: At that time General of Pacifying the North and garrison commander of Huaishuo Yang Jun memorialized: "It is reported that they have already set up a ruler, a cousin of Anagui on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifying North General and Huaishuo commander Yang Jun wrote, "Word comes that they have already enthroned a ruler—Anagui's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 夷人獸心，已相君長，恐未肯以殺兄之人，郊迎其弟。

translations.literal: Barbarians have the hearts of beasts; they have already accepted one lord and will hardly welcome at the suburbs the younger brother of the man who killed him.
translations.idiomatic: These barbarians have beasts' hearts; they already have a chief and will hardly greet the brother of the man they slew.

sentences.zh: 輕往虛反，徒損國威。

translations.literal: To go lightly would be futile and would only damage the state's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: A light return would come to nothing and only shame our realm.

sentences.zh: 自非廣加兵眾，無以送其入北。」

translations.literal: Unless we send a large force we cannot escort him north."
translations.idiomatic: Without a great army we cannot see him safely home."

sentences.zh: 二月，明帝詔舊經蠕蠕，使者牒雲具仁往，喻婆羅門迎阿那瑰復籓之意。

translations.literal: In the second month Emperor Ming ordered the former Rouran envoy Jururen to go and explain to Faboluomen the wish to welcome Anagui back to tributary status.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor sent the former Rouran envoy Jururen to tell Faboluomen that Wei wished to restore Anagui as a tributary king.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門殊自驕慢，無遜避之心，責具仁禮敬，具仁執節不屈。

translations.literal: Faboluomen was exceedingly arrogant, without deference; he demanded Jururen's courtesy, and Jururen held to protocol without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Faboluomen was insolent and showed no deference; he demanded Jururen's obeisance, and Jururen held to his staff unbowed.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門遣大官莫何去汾、俟斤丘升頭六人，將兵二千隨具仁迎阿那瑰。

translations.literal: Faboluomen sent the great officer Moguhui Qin, Houjin Qiushangtou, and six others with two thousand troops to accompany Jururen in welcoming Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: Faboluomen sent the great officer Moguhui Qin, Houjin Qiushangtou, and six others with two thousand horse to accompany Jururen and receive Anagui.

sentences.zh: 五月，具仁還鎮，論彼事勢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jururen returned to the garrison and reported on conditions there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jururen returned to the frontier post and reported what he had seen.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰慮不敢入，表求還京。

translations.literal: Anagui, fearing to enter, memorialized asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui, afraid to go in, petitioned to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會婆羅門為高車所逐，率十部落詣涼州歸降。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Faboluomen was driven out by the Gaoche and led ten tribes to Liangzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Faboluomen was driven off by the Gaoche and brought ten tribes to Liangzhou to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是蠕蠕數萬，相率迎阿那瑰。

translations.literal: Thereupon tens of thousands of Rouran came in succession to welcome Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: Then tens of thousands of Rouran came in waves to welcome Anagui.

sentences.zh: 七月，阿那瑰啟云：「投化阿那瑰蠕蠕元退社、渾河旃等二人，以今月二十六日到鎮，雲國土大亂，姓姓別住，迭相抄掠，當今北人，鵠望待拯。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Anagui submitted: "The surrendered Anagui's Rouran Yuan Tuishe and Hunhe Zhan and two others reached the garrison on the twenty-sixth of this month, reporting that the country is in great disorder, clans living apart and raiding one another; the northerners now crane their necks awaiting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Anagui wrote, "Two of my men, Yuan Tuishe and Hunhe Zhan, reached the garrison on the twenty-sixth and report that the realm is torn apart, clans raiding one another, and the northern people waiting desperately for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 今乞依前恩，賜給精兵一萬，還令督率領，送臣磧北，撫定荒人。

translations.literal: I now beg, according to your former grace, ten thousand picked troops to lead and escort me north of the desert to pacify the wild peoples.
translations.idiomatic: I beg, as before, ten thousand elite troops to lead me beyond the sands and settle the scattered tribes.

sentences.zh: 脫蒙所請，事必克濟。」

translations.literal: If this request is granted, the affair will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If you grant this, the task will surely succeed."

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書、門下博議。

translations.literal: The edict ordered the Ministry of State and the Secretariat to deliberate broadly.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the ministries to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔兼散騎常侍王遵業馳驛宣旨慰喻阿那瑰，並申賜賚。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the edict ordered Concurrent Cadet of the Irregular Cavalry Wang Zunye to ride post-haste with imperial words to comfort and instruct Anagui and announce further gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Zunye was sent post-haste with the emperor's words of comfort and further gifts.

sentences.zh: 九月，蠕蠕後主俟匿伐來奔懷朔鎮，阿那瑰兄也，列稱規望乞軍，並請阿那瑰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the former Rouran ruler Hou Nifa came to surrender at Huaishuo—Anagui's elder brother—stating his hopes and begging for troops, and also asking for Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the former Rouran ruler Hou Nifa, Anagui's elder brother, came to Huaishuo to submit, pleading for troops and for Anagui.

sentences.zh: 十月，錄尚書事高陽王雍、尚書令李崇、侍中侯剛、尚書左僕射元欽、侍中元叉、侍中安豐王延明、吏部尚書元修義、尚書李彥、給事黃門侍郎元纂、給事黃門侍郎張烈、給事黃門侍序盧同等奏曰：「竊聞漢立南北單于，晉有東西之稱，皆所以相維禦難，為國籓籬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Recorder of Affairs Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Minister of State Li Chong, Palace Attendant Hou Gang, Left Vice Director Yuan Qin, Palace Attendant Yuan Cha, Palace Attendant Prince of Anfeng Yanming, Minister of Civil Office Yuan Xiuyi, Minister of State Li Yan, Cadet of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, Cadet of the Yellow Gate Zhang Lie, Cadet of the Yellow Gate Lu Tong and others memorialized: "We have heard that Han set up northern and southern Shanyu, and Jin had eastern and western titles—all to support and defend against hardship as bulwarks of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month a roster of high ministers memorialized: "Han set up northern and southern Shanyu; Jin divided east and west—all to brace the realm as frontier shields.

sentences.zh: 今臣等參議，以為懷朔鎮北，土名無結山吐若奚泉，敦煌北西海郡，即漢、晉舊鄣，二處寬平，原野彌沃。

translations.literal: We deliberated and believe that north of Huaishuo is a place called Wujieshan Turuoxi Spring, and north of Dunhuang is Xihai Commandery, the old Han and Jin frontier posts—both broad and level, with fertile plains.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that north of Huaishuo lies Turuoxi Spring at Wujie Mountain, and west of Dunhuang the old Han and Jin post of Xihai—both broad lands with rich pasture.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰宜置西吐若奚泉，婆羅門宜置西海郡。

translations.literal: Anagui should be placed at Turuoxi Spring in the west; Faboluomen at Xihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui should settle at western Turuoxi Spring; Faboluomen at Xihai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 各令總率部落，收離聚散。

translations.literal: Each should command his tribes and gather the scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Each should gather his tribes and rally the dispersed.

sentences.zh: 其爵號及資給所須，唯恩裁處。

translations.literal: Titles and needed supplies are for Your Majesty's grace alone to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and provisions rest with Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 彼臣下之官，任其舊俗。

translations.literal: Officials among their subjects may keep their old customs.
translations.idiomatic: Their subordinate offices may keep barbarian custom.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰所居既是境外，宜少優遣，以示威刑。

translations.literal: Since Anagui's dwelling is beyond the border, he should receive somewhat lighter dispatch to display majesty and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Because Anagui dwells beyond the border, his escort should be modest yet show imperial sternness.

sentences.zh: 計沃野、懷朔、武川鎮各差二百人，令當鎮軍主監率，給其糧仗，送至前所。

translations.literal: It is calculated that Woye, Huaishuo, and Wuchuan garrisons should each detach two hundred men, with the garrison commander supervising, supplying grain and arms and escorting them to the appointed place.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the garrisons at Woye, Huaishuo, and Wuchuan should send two hundred men under their commanders with grain and weapons to escort them thither.

sentences.zh: 仍於彼為其造構，功就聽還。

translations.literal: They should also build structures for them there; when the work is done they may return.
translations.idiomatic: They should build camps for them there, then return when the work is done.

sentences.zh: 諸於北來在婆羅門前投化者，令州鎮上佐，准程給糧，送詣懷朔阿那瑰，鎮與使人，量給食稟；

translations.literal: All who come from the north to submit before Faboluomen should have the prefecture and garrison senior aide supply grain by regulation and send them to Anagui at Huaishuo; the garrison should give envoys rations as measured;
translations.idiomatic: Northerners who submit before Faboluomen should be fed by local officials and sent on to Anagui at Huaishuo; garrisons should ration the envoys;

sentences.zh: 在京館者，任其去留。

translations.literal: those lodged in the capital may stay or leave as they wish.
translations.idiomatic: those lodged in the capital may come or go as they please.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰草創，先無儲積，請給朔州麻子乾飯二千斛，官駝運送。

translations.literal: Anagui is just beginning and has no stores; we request two thousand hu of hemp-seed dried grain from Shuozhou, transported by government camels.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui has no stores at the start; grant two thousand hu of hemp-seed grain from Shuozhou, carried by imperial camels.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門居於四海，既是境內，資衛不得同之。

translations.literal: Faboluomen dwells within the four seas and is within the borders; his supplies cannot be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Faboluomen lies within the realm; his allowance cannot match Anagui's.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰等新造籓屏，宜各遣使持節馳驛，先詣慰喻，並委經略。」

translations.literal: Anagui and the others, newly made frontier shields, should each have an envoy with staff sent post-haste to comfort and instruct them first and entrust overall planning."
translations.idiomatic: As new frontier shields, each should receive an envoy sent ahead to comfort them and oversee arrangements."

sentences.zh: 明帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔安西將軍、廷尉元洪超兼尚書行台，詣敦煌安置婆羅門。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the edict ordered General of Pacifying the West and Minister of Justice Yuan Hongchao, concurrently Minister of State on the mobile secretariat, to go to Dunhuang to settle Faboluomen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yuan Hongchao was sent to Dunhuang to settle Faboluomen.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門尋與部眾謀叛投嚈噠。

translations.literal: Before long Faboluomen plotted with his tribes to rebel and flee to the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Faboluomen plotted with his followers to defect to the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 嚈噠三妻，皆婆羅門姊妹也。

translations.literal: The Yeda king had three wives, all Faboluomen's sisters.
translations.idiomatic: The Yeda king's three wives were all Faboluomen's sisters.

sentences.zh: 仍為州軍所討，禽之。

translations.literal: He was thereupon punished by the provincial army and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops overtook and seized him.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，阿那瑰上表，乞粟以為田種。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year Anagui memorialized, begging grain for seed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year Anagui asked for seed grain.

sentences.zh: 詔給萬石。

translations.literal: The edict granted ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand shi were granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，阿那瑰眾大饑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Anagui's masses suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his people were stricken with famine.

sentences.zh: 入塞寇抄。

translations.literal: They entered the frontier to raid.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the border to plunder.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔尚書左丞元孚兼行台尚書，持節喻之，孚見阿那瑰。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming ordered Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Yuan Fu, concurrently mobile secretariat minister with staff, to go instruct him; Fu met Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuan Fu with imperial staff to admonish him; Fu met Anagui.

sentences.zh: 為其所執。

translations.literal: He was seized by him.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui seized him.

sentences.zh: 以孚自隨，驅掠良口二千並公私驛馬、牛羊數十萬北遁，謝孚放還。

translations.literal: Taking Fu with him, he drove off two thousand good subjects and public and private post horses and cattle and sheep by the hundreds of thousands northward, then released Fu and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He took Fu along, swept off two thousand subjects and countless post horses, cattle, and sheep to the north, then released Fu.

sentences.zh: 詔驃騎大將軍、尚書令李崇等率騎十萬討之，出塞三千餘里，至瀚海，不及而還。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Valiant Cavalry General and Minister of State Li Chong and others to lead 100,000 horse against him; they went more than 3,000 li beyond the frontier to the Han Sea but could not catch him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was sent with a hundred thousand horse in pursuit; they marched three thousand li to the Han Sea, failed to overtake him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 俟匿伐至洛陽，明帝臨西堂引見之。

translations.literal: When Hou Nifa reached Luoyang, Emperor Ming received him at the Western Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Nifa reached Luoyang, the emperor received him at the Western Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年，婆羅門死于洛南之館，詔贈使持節、鎮西將軍、秦州刺史、廣牧公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Faboluomen died at the lodge south of the Luo; the edict posthumously appointed him Staff with Golden Tassel, General of Pacifying the West, Governor of Qinzhou, and Duke of Guangmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Faboluomen died at the southern lodge; he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Guangmu with the rank of General of Pacifying the West.

sentences.zh: 是歲，沃野鎮人破六韓拔陵反，諸鎮相應。

translations.literal: That year the people of Woye Garrison, Poliuhan Baling, rebelled and the garrisons responded one after another.
translations.idiomatic: That year Poliuhan Baling of Woye Garrison rebelled and the other garrisons rose in turn.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年春，阿那瑰率眾討之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiaochang, Anagui led his masses to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Xiaochang, Anagui marched against them.

sentences.zh: 詔遣牒雲具仁齎雜物勞賜。

translations.literal: The edict sent Dieyun Jururen bearing mixed goods to comfort and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Dieyun Jururen was sent with gifts to reward him.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰拜受詔命，勒眾十萬，從武川鎮西向沃野，頻戰克捷。

translations.literal: Anagui received the edict, mustered 100,000 men, marched west from Wuchuan Garrison toward Woye, and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui took the edict, raised a hundred thousand men, marched west from Wuchuan toward Woye, and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 四月，明帝又遣通直散騎常侍、中書舍人馮俊使阿那瑰，宣勞班賜有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Emperor Ming again sent Direct Cadet of the Irregular Cavalry and Secretariat Attendant Feng Jun to Anagui to proclaim comfort and graded rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Feng Jun was sent to proclaim the court's praise and graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰部落既和，土馬稍盛，乃號敕連頭兵伐可汗，魏言把攬也。

translations.literal: Anagui's tribes being at peace, horses and herds grew somewhat; he styled himself Khaghan Chiletoubingfa—in Wei speech, "to grasp and hold."
translations.idiomatic: His tribes at peace and his herds growing, he styled himself Khaghan Chiletoubingfa—"he who seizes and holds," in the Wei tongue.

sentences.zh: 十月，阿那瑰復遣鬱久閭彌娥等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Anagui again sent Yujiuli Mi'e and others with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he again sent Mi'e and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，阿那瑰遣人鞏鳳景等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Anagui sent Gong Fengjing and others with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Gong Fengjing and others to court.

sentences.zh: 及還，明帝詔之曰：「北鎮群狄，為逆不息，蠕蠕主為國立忠，助加誅討，言念誠心，無忘寢食。

translations.literal: On their return Emperor Ming charged them: "The northern garrisons' barbarians rebel without cease; the Rouran king has shown loyalty to the state and aided in punishment—thinking of his sincere heart, I cannot forget it even in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the emperor told them, "The northern tribes rebel endlessly; your king has served the state faithfully in punishing them—his loyalty keeps me wakeful at night.

sentences.zh: 今知停在朔垂，與爾硃榮鄰接，其嚴勒部曲，勿相暴掠。

translations.literal: We now know he halts at the northern fringe, neighboring Erzhu Rong; strictly restrain your bands and do not plunder one another.
translations.idiomatic: We hear he camps on the northern marches near Erzhu Rong; tell him to restrain his men from mutual plunder.

sentences.zh: 又近得蠕蠕主啟，更欲為國東討。

translations.literal: We have lately received the Rouran king's petition that he wishes again to campaign east for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He has lately asked to campaign east again on our behalf.

sentences.zh: 但蠕蠕主世居北漠，不宜炎夏，今可且停，聽待後敕。」

translations.literal: But the Rouran king has always dwelt in the northern desert and is unsuited to hot summers; for now let him halt and await further orders."
translations.idiomatic: But his people belong in the northern desert, not the summer heat—let him wait for further orders."

sentences.zh: 蓋朝廷慮其反覆也。

translations.literal: This was because the court feared his fickleness.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared his fickleness.

sentences.zh: 此後頻使朝貢。

translations.literal: After this he sent tribute frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute came often.

sentences.zh: 建義初，孝莊詔曰：「夫勳高者賞重，德厚者名隆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Emperor Xiaozhuang's edict said: "Heavy merit deserves heavy reward; deep virtue deserves a lofty name.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianyi, Emperor Xiaozhuang proclaimed, "Great merit demands great reward; deep virtue, a lofty name.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瑰鎮衛北籓，禦侮朔表，遂使陰山息警，弱水無塵，刊跡狼山，銘名瀚海。

translations.literal: The Rouran king Anagui guards the northern frontier, repelling insult on the northern marches, so that Mount Yin rests from alarms and the Weak Waters know no dust; he carved his track on Wolf Mountain and inscribed his name on the Han Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui guards the northern marches so that Yinshan is quiet and the Weak Waters still; he has carved his name on Wolf Mountain and the Han Sea.

sentences.zh: 至誠既篤，勳緒莫酬，故宜標以殊禮，何容格以恆式。

translations.literal: His sincerity is profound and his achievements cannot be repaid; therefore extraordinary rites are fitting—how can ordinary forms suffice?
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty is profound and his service beyond repayment; extraordinary rites are fitting—ordinary forms will not do.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，贊拜不言名，上書不稱臣。」

translations.literal: From now on, in congratulatory bows do not speak his name; in memorials to the throne do not style himself subject."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth he need not speak his name in court bows, nor call himself subject in memorials."

sentences.zh: 太昌元年六月，阿那瑰遣烏勾蘭樹升伐等朝貢，並為長子請尚公主。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Taichang, Anagui sent Wugoulan Shushengfa and others with tribute and asked that a princess be given to his eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Taichang year one he sent Shushengfa and others with tribute and asked a princess for his eldest son.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年四月，孝武詔以范陽王誨之長女琅曁邪公主許之，未及成婚，帝入關。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Xiaowu decreed that the eldest daughter of Prince of Fanyang Hui, Princess Langye, be betrothed to him; before the marriage could take place the emperor entered Guan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongxi year two Emperor Xiaowu betrothed Princess Langye, daughter of the Prince of Fanyang, to him; before the wedding the emperor fled into Guan.

sentences.zh: 東、西魏競結阿那瑰為婚好。

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Wei competed to bind Anagui by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Wei both courted him with marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 西魏文帝乃以孝武時舍人元翌女稱為化政公主，妻阿那瑰兄弟塔寒，又自納阿那瑰女為後，加以金帛誘之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Western Wei therefore gave the daughter of the attendant Yuan Yi from Emperor Xiaowu's time, styled Princess Huazheng, in marriage to Anagui's brother Tahan, and himself took Anagui's daughter as empress, adding gold and silk to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei's Emperor Wen gave Yuan Yi's daughter, styled Princess Huazheng, to Anagui's brother Tahan, took Anagui's daughter as empress, and heaped gold and silk upon them.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰遂留東魏使元整，不報信命。

translations.literal: Anagui thereupon detained Eastern Wei's envoy Yuan Zheng and sent no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui detained Eastern Wei's envoy Yuan Zheng and sent no answer.

sentences.zh: 後遂率眾度河，又廢後為言，文帝不得已，遂敕廢後自殺。

translations.literal: Later he led his masses across the river and, using the deposition of his daughter as a pretext, Emperor Wen had no choice but to order the deposed empress to kill herself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he crossed the Yellow River; using his daughter's deposition as pretext, Emperor Wen was forced to order the empress to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 元象元年五月，阿那瑰掠幽州范陽，南至易水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yuanxiang, Anagui raided Fanyang in Youzhou, south to Yishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yuanxiang year one he raided Fanyang in Youzhou as far south as Yishui.

sentences.zh: 九月，又掠肆州秀容，至於三推。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again raided Xiurong in Sizhou, reaching Santui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he raided Xiurong in Sizhou to Santui.

sentences.zh: 又殺元整，轉謀侵害。

translations.literal: He also killed Yuan Zheng and turned to plotting aggression.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Yuan Zheng and turned to open aggression.

sentences.zh: 東魏乃囚阿那瑰使溫豆拔等。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei thereupon imprisoned Anagui's envoys Wendouba and others.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei imprisoned his envoys Wendouba and others.

sentences.zh: 祖武以阿那瑰凶狡，將撫懷之，乃遣其使人龍無駒北還，以通溫豆拔等音問。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Qi, because Anagui was fierce and cunning yet wished to win him over, sent his envoy Long Wuju north to restore contact with Wendouba and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Emperor Wen, wishing to win him despite his treachery, sent Long Wuju north to contact the imprisoned envoys.

sentences.zh: 始阿那瑰殺元整，亦謂溫豆拔等不存，既見無駒，微懷感愧。

translations.literal: At first, when Anagui killed Yuan Zheng, he thought Wendouba and the others were gone; seeing Wuju, he felt a slight shame.
translations.idiomatic: He had thought Wendouba dead; seeing Wuju, he felt a twinge of shame.

sentences.zh: 興和二年春，復遣龍無駒等朝貢東魏。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Xinghe he again sent Long Wuju and others with tribute to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xinghe year two he again sent Long Wuju to Eastern Wei with tribute.

sentences.zh: 然猶未款誠。

translations.literal: Yet he was still not sincerely submissive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his submission was still not sincere.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰女妻文帝者遇疾死，齊神武因遣相府功曹參軍張徽纂使于阿那瑰，間說之。

translations.literal: Anagui's daughter who had married Emperor Wen died of illness; Qi Emperor Shenwu therefore sent Zhang Huizuan of the chancellor's staff to Anagui to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: When the daughter who had married Emperor Wen died, Qi Emperor Shenwu sent Zhang Huizuan to win him over.

sentences.zh: 雲文帝及周文既害孝武，又殺阿那瑰之女，妄以疏屬假公主之號，嫁彼為親。

translations.literal: He said Emperor Wen and Zhou Emperor Wen had both killed Emperor Xiaowu and also killed Anagui's daughter, falsely giving a distant kinswoman the title of princess and marrying her to them as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said Western Wei had murdered Emperor Xiaowu and Anagui's daughter, then palmed off a distant cousin as a princess.

sentences.zh: 又阿那瑰度河西討時，周文燒草，使其馬饑，不得南進，此其逆詐反覆難信之狀。

translations.literal: Moreover when Anagui crossed the river west to campaign, Zhou Emperor Wen burned the grass so his horses starved and he could not advance south—such is their deceitful, fickle, untrustworthy conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui crossed west to campaign, Zhou Wen burned the pasture so his horses starved—proof of their treachery.

sentences.zh: 又論東魏正統所在，言其往者破亡歸命，魏朝保護，得存其國，以大義示之。

translations.literal: He also spoke of where Eastern Wei's orthodox legitimacy lay, saying that in former days when they were broken and fled to surrender, the Wei court protected them and preserved their state—showing them the greater righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of Eastern Wei as the true succession, reminding Anagui that Wei had once preserved his broken realm—appealing to gratitude and right.

sentences.zh: 兼詐阿那瑰云：近有赤鋪步落堅胡行於河西，為蠕蠕主所獲。

translations.literal: He also deceived Anagui, saying that recently a Boluobuluoian Hu had traveled in the Hexi and was seized by the Rouran king.
translations.idiomatic: He also told a tale of a Hu traveler seized in the Hexi by the Rouran king.

sentences.zh: 雲蠕蠕主問之：「汝從高王？

translations.literal: He said the Rouran king asked him: "Do you follow the High King?
translations.idiomatic: The king had asked the man, "Do you serve the High King?

sentences.zh: 為從黑獺？」

translations.literal: Or do you follow the Black Badger?"
translations.idiomatic: Or the Black Badger?"

sentences.zh: 一人言從黑獺，蠕蠕主殺之；

translations.literal: One man said he followed the Black Badger, and the Rouran king killed him;
translations.idiomatic: One said the Black Badger, and was killed;

sentences.zh: 二人言從高王，蠕蠕主放遣。

translations.literal: two men said they followed the High King, and the Rouran king released them.
translations.idiomatic: two said the High King, and were released.

sentences.zh: 此即蠕蠕主存大國宿昔仁義。

translations.literal: This shows the Rouran king's long-standing righteousness in preserving a great state.
translations.idiomatic: This, he said, showed the Rouran king's old loyalty to a great ally.

sentences.zh: 彼女既見害，欺詐相待，不仁不信，宜見討伐。

translations.literal: Since his daughter was harmed and they dealt with him by fraud without benevolence or faith, they should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: They had harmed his daughter and dealt in fraud—such men deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 且守逆一方，未知歸順，朝廷亦欲加誅。

translations.literal: Moreover they hold to rebellion in one corner, their submission unknown; the court also means to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: They held a rebel corner of the realm; the court too meant to strike them.

sentences.zh: 彼若深念舊恩，以存和睦，當以天子懿親公主結成姻媾，為遣兵將，伐彼叛臣，為蠕蠕主雪恥報惡。

translations.literal: If he deeply recalls old kindness and wishes to preserve harmony, let an imperial princess of the Son of Heaven's own kin be joined in marriage, and troops be sent to campaign against their rebel ministers and avenge the Rouran king's wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: If Anagui cherished old kindness, let an imperial princess wed his house and Eastern Wei send troops to avenge his wrongs.

sentences.zh: 徽纂既申齊神武意，阿那瑰乃召其大臣與議之，便歸誠於東魏。

translations.literal: Huizuan having conveyed Qi Emperor Shenwu's intent, Anagui summoned his great ministers to deliberate and thereupon submitted sincerely to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizuan had spoken for Shenwu, Anagui consulted his chiefs and turned sincerely to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 遣其俟利、莫何莫緣游大力等朝貢，因為其子庵羅辰請婚。

translations.literal: He sent his Houli, Mohemoyuan Youdali, and others with tribute and asked marriage for his son Anluochen.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Youdali and others with tribute and asked a bride for his son Anluochen.

sentences.zh: 靜帝詔兼散騎常侍太府卿羅念、兼通直散騎常侍中書舍人穆景相等使于阿那瑰。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing decreed Concurrent Cadet of the Irregular Cavalry and Grand Steward Luo Nian and Concurrent Direct Cadet of the Irregular Cavalry and Secretariat Attendant Mu Jingxiang as envoys to Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing sent Luo Nian and Mu Jingxiang as envoys to him.

sentences.zh: 八月，阿那瑰遣莫何去折豆渾十升等朝貢，復因求婚。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Anagui sent Moguhui Zhedouhun Shisheng and others with tribute, again asking for marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Shisheng and others with tribute and again asked for marriage.

sentences.zh: 齊神武請遂其意，以招四遠。

translations.literal: Qi Emperor Shenwu asked that his wish be granted to win the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu urged that the match be made to win the distant tribes.

sentences.zh: 詔以常山王騭妹樂安公主許之，改封為蘭陵郡長公主。

translations.literal: The edict betrothed the sister of Prince of Changshan Zhi, Princess Le'an, to him, changing her title to Princess of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Le'an, sister of the Prince of Changshan, was betrothed to him and ennobled Princess of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 十二月，阿那瑰復遣折豆渾十升詣東魏請婚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Anagui again sent Zhedouhun Shisheng to Eastern Wei to request the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he again sent Shisheng to request the wedding.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，阿那瑰遣吐豆登鬱久閭譬渾、俊利莫何折豆常侯煩等奉馬千疋，以為聘禮，請迎公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Anagui sent Tudeng Yujiuli Pihun, Junli Mohe Zhedouchanghou Fan, and others with a thousand horses as betrothal gifts, asking to receive the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year three he sent a thousand horses as bride-price and asked that the princess be sent.

sentences.zh: 詔兼宗正卿元壽、兼太常卿孟韶等送公主自晉陽北邁，資用器物，齊神武親自經紀，咸出豐渥。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Shou and Concurrent Director of Imperial Sacrifices Meng Shao and others to escort the princess north from Jinyang; supplies and utensils were personally arranged by Qi Emperor Shenwu, all from splendid stores.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shou and Meng Shao escorted the princess north from Jinyang; Shenwu himself oversaw a lavish trousseau.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰遣其吐豆登鬱久閭匿伏、俊利阿夷普掘、蒱提棄之伏等迎公主于新城之南。

translations.literal: Anagui sent his Tudeng Yujiuli Yinfu, Junli Ayipujue, Puti Qizhifu, and others to meet the princess south of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui sent Yinfu, Ayipujue, and others to meet the princess south of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，齊神武慮阿那瑰難信，又以國事加重，躬送公主于樓煩之北，接勞其使，每皆隆厚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Qi Emperor Shenwu, fearing Anagui's untrustworthiness and also because state affairs were weighty, personally escorted the princess north of Loufan, receiving and comforting the envoys with great generosity each time.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Shenwu, doubting Anagui's faith, personally escorted the princess north of Loufan and lavished honor on every envoy.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰大喜，自是朝貢東魏相尋。

translations.literal: Anagui was greatly pleased; from this tribute to Eastern Wei followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui was overjoyed; tribute to Eastern Wei flowed without cease.

sentences.zh: 四年，阿那瑰請以其孫女號鄰和公主妻齊神武第九子長廣公湛，靜帝詔為婚焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Anagui asked that his granddaughter, styled Princess Linhe, marry the ninth son of Qi Emperor Shenwu, Duke of Changgong Zhan; Emperor Jing decreed the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked that his granddaughter Princess Linhe wed Shenwu's ninth son, Duke Zhan of Changgong; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰遣其吐豆登鬱久閭譬掘、俊利莫何遊大刀送女于晉陽。

translations.literal: Anagui sent his Tudeng Yujiuli Pijue, Junli Mohe Youdadao, and others to escort the girl to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pijue, Youdadao, and others to bring the girl to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 武定四年，阿那瑰有愛女，號為公主，以齊神武威德日盛，又請致之，靜帝聞而詔神武納之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding, Anagui had a beloved daughter styled princess; because Qi Emperor Shenwu's martial virtue grew daily stronger, he asked to send her too; Emperor Jing heard and decreed that Shenwu take her.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wuding he had another beloved daughter whom, seeing Shenwu's power grow, he offered to the court; Emperor Jing ordered Shenwu to accept her.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰遣其吐豆發鬱久閭汗拔姻姬等送女于晉陽。

translations.literal: Anagui sent his Tudengfa Yujiuli Hanbayinyiji and others to escort the girl to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hanbayinyiji and others to escort her to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 自此東魏邊塞無事，至於武定末，使貢相尋。

translations.literal: From this the Eastern Wei frontier was untroubled; until the end of Wuding envoys and tribute followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Eastern Wei border knew peace; through the end of the Wuding era tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 始阿那瑰初復其國，盡禮朝廷。

translations.literal: At first when Anagui restored his state he was fully observant toward the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui first restored his realm he observed every courtesy toward the court.

sentences.zh: 明帝之後，中原喪亂，未能外略，阿那瑰統率北方，頗為強盛，稍敢驕大，禮敬頗闕，遣使朝貢，不復稱臣。

translations.literal: After Emperor Ming, the central plains fell into disorder and could not attend to external campaigns; Anagui commanded the north and grew quite powerful, gradually daring arrogance; courtesy and respect were much lacking, and though he sent envoys with tribute he no longer styled himself subject.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming the heartland collapsed in chaos; Anagui grew mighty in the north, turned proud, slackened in courtesy, and though he still sent tribute he no longer called himself subject.

sentences.zh: 天平以來，逾自踞慢。

translations.literal: From the Tianping era onward he became ever more haughty and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianping era on he grew ever more insolent.

sentences.zh: 汝陽王暹之為秦州也，遣其典簽齊人淳于覃使于阿那瑰。

translations.literal: When Prince of Ruyang Xian was in Qinzhou, he sent his registrar, the Qi man Chunyu Tan, as envoy to Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ruyang, Xian, governed Qinzhou, he sent his registrar Chunyu Tan, a man of Qi, to Anagui.

sentences.zh: 遂留之，親寵任事。

translations.literal: Anagui detained him and favored him with intimate trust in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui kept him and favored him with intimate trust.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰因入洛陽，心慕中國，立官號，僭擬王者，遂有侍中、黃門之屬。

translations.literal: Because Anagui had entered Luoyang and admired China, he established offices and titles, arrogating to kingly forms, and had attendants such as Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Having seen Luoyang he admired China, set up offices, aped a king's court, and kept attendants and secretaries like a Chinese ruler.

sentences.zh: 以覃為秘書監、黃門郎，掌其文墨。

translations.literal: He made Tan Director of the Secretariat and Yellow Gate Attendant, in charge of his documents.
translations.idiomatic: He made Tan Director of the Secretariat and Yellow Gate Attendant, keeper of his records.

sentences.zh: 覃教阿那瑰，轉至不遜，每奉國書，鄰敵抗禮。

translations.literal: Tan taught Anagui to become ever more insolent; each time he presented state letters he used the protocol due a neighboring equal.
translations.idiomatic: Tan taught him insolence; in every state letter he claimed the standing of an equal neighbor.

sentences.zh: 及齊受東魏禪，亦歲時往來不絕。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication from Eastern Wei, yearly intercourse also never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi succeeded Eastern Wei, envoys still came and went each year.

sentences.zh: 天保三年，阿那瑰為突厥所破，自殺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, Anagui was broken by the Turks and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao the Turks broke him and he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 其太子庵羅辰及瑰從弟登注俟利、登注子庫提，並擁眾奔齊。

translations.literal: His crown prince Anluochen and Anagui's cousin Dengzhu Houli, Dengzhu's son Kuti, all led their masses to flee to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Anluochen, his cousin Dengzhu Houli, and Houli's son Kuti all fled to Qi with their followers.

sentences.zh: 其餘眾立注次子鐵伐為主。

translations.literal: The remainder set up Zhuzi's son Tiefa as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant tribes raised Zhuzi's son Tiefa.

sentences.zh: 四年，齊文宣送登注及子庫提還北。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Qi Emperor Wenxuan sent Dengzhu and his son Kuti back north.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wenxuan sent Dengzhu and Kuti back north.

sentences.zh: 鐵伐尋為契丹所殺，其國人仍立登注為主。

translations.literal: Before long Tiefa was killed by the Khitan; his people again set up Dengzhu as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tiefa was killed by the Khitan and Dengzhu was raised again.

sentences.zh: 又為大人阿富提等所殺，其國人復立庫提為主。

translations.literal: He was again killed by the great chief Afuti and others; the people again set up Kuti as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Afuti and other chiefs killed him in turn; the people raised Kuti.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復為突厥所攻，舉國奔齊。

translations.literal: That year they were again attacked by the Turks; the whole nation fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Turks struck again and the whole nation fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 文宣乃北討突厥，迎納蠕蠕，廢其主庫提，立阿那瑰子庵羅辰為主，致之馬邑川，給其廩餼、繒帛。

translations.literal: Wenxuan thereupon campaigned north against the Turks, received the Rouran, deposed Kuti, set Anagui's son Anluochen as ruler, and settled them at Mayi River, supplying grain rations and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan marched north against the Turks, received the Rouran, deposed Kuti, installed Anluochen, and settled them at Mayi River with grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 親追突厥于朔方，突厥請降，許之而還。

translations.literal: He personally pursued the Turks to Shuofang; the Turks asked to surrender and he accepted and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the Turks to Shuofang; they sued for peace and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是蠕蠕貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rouran tribute was unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran tribute flowed without interruption.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，庵羅辰叛，文宣親討，大破之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Anluochen rebelled; Wenxuan personally campaigned and routed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Anluochen rebelled; Wenxuan took the field and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 庵羅辰父子北遁。

translations.literal: Anluochen and his son fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Anluochen and his son fled north.

sentences.zh: 四月，寇肆州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they raided Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they raided Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝自晉陽討之，至恆州黃瓜堆，虜散走。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned from Jinyang to Hengzhou Huangguadui; the barbarians scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched from Jinyang to Huangguadui in Hengzhou; the enemy scattered.

sentences.zh: 時大軍已還。

translations.literal: At that time the great army had already returned.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 帝麾下千餘騎，遇蠕蠕別部數萬，四面圍逼。

translations.literal: The emperor had a thousand odd horse in his escort and met several tens of thousands of a separate Rouran division, surrounded on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: With barely a thousand horse he met tens of thousands of a Rouran splinter band and was ringed on every side.

sentences.zh: 帝神色自若，指畫形勢，虜眾披靡，遂縱兵潰圍而出。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression was calm as he pointed out the situation; the barbarian masses wavered, and he thereupon loosed his troops and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: His face never changed as he directed the fight; the enemy wavered and he burst through the ring.

sentences.zh: 虜退走，追擊之，伏屍二十五里，獲庵羅辰妻子及生口三萬餘人。

translations.literal: The barbarians retreated; pursuing them, corpses lay for twenty-five li; they captured Anluochen's wife and children and more than thirty thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing foe for twenty-five li of corpses and took Anluochen's family and more than thirty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝又北討蠕蠕，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor again campaigned north against the Rouran and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he marched north again and broke the Rouran utterly.

sentences.zh: 六月，蠕蠕帥部眾東徙，將南侵，帝帥輕騎于金川下邀擊，蠕蠕聞而遠遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Rouran chief led his tribes eastward, intending to invade south; the emperor with light horse intercepted them at Jinchuan; hearing this the Rouran fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month their chief moved east intending to raid south; Wenxuan intercepted him at Jinchuan with light horse and the Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，文宣又親討蠕蠕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year Wenxuan again personally campaigned against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year he campaigned against them again in person.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝頓白道，留輜重，親率輕騎五千追蠕蠕，躬犯矢石，頻大破之，遂至沃野，大獲而還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor halted at Baidao, left baggage, and personally led five thousand light horse in pursuit, himself braving arrows and stones, repeatedly routing them greatly, reaching Woye, and returning with great spoils.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he left his baggage at Baidao, led five thousand light horse in pursuit, took arrow and stone himself, routed them again and again to Woye, and returned laden with spoil.

sentences.zh: 是時，蠕蠕既累為突厥所破，以西魏恭帝二年，遂率部千餘家奔關中。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran, having repeatedly been broken by the Turks, in the second year of Western Wei's Emperor Gong led more than a thousand households to flee into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Broken repeatedly by the Turks, in Western Wei's second year of Emperor Gong more than a thousand Rouran households fled into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 突厥既恃兵強，又藉西魏和好，恐其遺類依憑大國，使驛相繼，請盡殺以甘心。

translations.literal: The Turks, relying on military strength and also on their good relations with Western Wei, feared the remnant would lean on a great state; messengers followed one another asking that all be killed to their satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, strong and allied with Western Wei, feared the survivors would cling to a great power and sent messenger after messenger demanding their deaths.

sentences.zh: 周文議許之，遂收縛蠕蠕主已下三千餘人付突厥使，於青門外斬之。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen deliberated and consented; they bound more than three thousand persons from the Rouran ruler down and handed them to the Turkish envoy, who beheaded them outside the Qing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Emperor Wen agreed; more than three thousand Rouran from the chief down were bound and beheaded outside the Qing Gate for the Turks.

sentences.zh: 中男以下免，並配王公家。

translations.literal: Those below middle age were spared and assigned to princely households.
translations.idiomatic: Those below middle age were spared and distributed among the princely houses.

sentences.zh: 匈奴宇文莫槐，出遼東塞外，其先南單于之遠屬也，世為東部大人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu came from beyond the Liaodong frontier; his ancestors were distant kin of the Southern Shanyu and for generations were great chiefs of the eastern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Mohuai of the Xiongnu came from beyond the Liaodong passes; his line were distant kin of the Southern Shanyu and for generations chiefs of the eastern tribes.

sentences.zh: 其語與鮮卑頗異。

translations.literal: Their language differed considerably from Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Their tongue differed markedly from Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 人皆翦發而留其頂上，以為首飾，長過數寸則截短之。

translations.literal: All cut their hair but left the crown, taking it as head ornament; when it grew more than several inches they cut it short.
translations.idiomatic: Men shaved the sides but left the crown as ornament, trimming it when it grew past a few inches.

sentences.zh: 婦女被長襦及足，而無裳焉。

translations.literal: Women wore long jackets reaching the feet but had no skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore long coats to the feet and wore no skirts.

sentences.zh: 秋收烏頭為毒藥，以射禽獸。

translations.literal: In autumn they gathered crow-dipper root as poison to shoot birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn they gathered aconite for poisoned arrows to hunt game.

sentences.zh: 莫槐虐用其人，為部下所殺，更立其弟普撥為大人。

translations.literal: Mohuai cruelly abused his people and was killed by his subordinates; they set up his younger brother Pubo as great chief.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuai tyrannized his people and was killed; his younger brother Pubo was raised up.

sentences.zh: 蓋撥死，子丘不勤立，尚平帝女。

translations.literal: When Pubo died, his son Qiubuqin succeeded and married an emperor of the Ping era's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When Pubo died his son Qiubuqin succeeded and wed a daughter of Emperor Ping.

sentences.zh: 兵不勤死，子莫廆立。

translations.literal: When Qiubuqin died, his son Mohui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiubuqin died his son Mohui took his place.

sentences.zh: 本名犯道武諱。

translations.literal: His original name violated Emperor Daowu's taboo.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name violated Emperor Daowu's taboo.

sentences.zh: 莫廆遣弟屈雲攻慕容廆，慕容廆擊破之。

translations.literal: Mohui sent his younger brother Quyun to attack Murong Hui; Murong Hui defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohui sent his brother Quyun against Murong Hui and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 又遣別部素延伐慕容廆於棘城，復為慕容廆所破，時莫廆部眾強盛，自稱單于，塞外諸部咸憚之。

translations.literal: He also sent a separate division, Suyan, to attack Murong Hui at Jicheng; he was again defeated by Murong Hui; at that time Mohui's tribes were powerful and he styled himself Shanyu; all tribes beyond the frontier feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Suyan against Murong Hui at Jicheng and was beaten again; Mohui's power was then at its height and he styled himself Shanyu, feared by every tribe beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 莫廆死，子遜昵延立，率眾攻慕容廆於棘城。

translations.literal: When Mohui died, his son Xunniyan succeeded and led his masses to attack Murong Hui at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Mohui died his son Xunniyan attacked Murong Hui at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 廆子翰先戍於外，遜昵延謂其眾曰：「翰素果勇，必為人患，宜先取之，城不足憂也。」

translations.literal: Hui's son Han was garrisoned outside; Xunniyan told his masses: "Han has always been resolute and brave and will surely be a menace—we should take him first; the city is no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Han held an outer camp; Xunniyan told his men, "Han is bold and dangerous—take him first; the city can wait."

sentences.zh: 乃分騎數千襲翰，翰聞之，使人詐為段末波使者，逆謂遜昵延曰：「翰數為吾患，久思除之，今聞來討，甚善。

translations.literal: He thereupon divided several thousand horse to strike Han; Han, hearing this, sent a man feigning to be an envoy of Duan Mobo, meeting Xunniyan and saying: "Han has long been our trouble and we have wished to remove him; hearing you come to punish him is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent several thousand horse against Han; Han feigned an envoy of Duan Mobo who told Xunniyan, "Han has long been our bane—we rejoice that you come to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 戒嚴相待，宜兼路早赴。」

translations.literal: Keep strict watch and come early by another road."
translations.idiomatic: Keep strict watch and come early by another road."

sentences.zh: 翰設伏待之。

translations.literal: Han set an ambush and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Han laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延以為信然。

translations.literal: Xunniyan believed it was true.
translations.idiomatic: Xunniyan believed every word.

sentences.zh: 長驅不備，至於伏所，為翰所虜。

translations.literal: He drove hard without precaution; reaching the ambush he was captured by Han.
translations.idiomatic: He charged carelessly into the trap and was seized.

sentences.zh: 翰馳使告，乘勝遂進，及晨而至。

translations.literal: Han sent a fast messenger to report; taking advantage of victory he pressed on and arrived at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent word and pressed on at dawn.

sentences.zh: 廆亦盡銳應之。

translations.literal: Hui also brought his full strength to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui marched out with his full strength.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延見而方嚴，率眾逆擊戰，前鋒始交，而翰已入其營，縱火燎之，眾乃大潰，遜昵延單馬奔還，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: Xunniyan saw the array and was just setting his troops to counterattack when the vanguard had barely joined; Han had already entered his camp and set fire; the masses broke in great rout; Xunniyan fled alone on horseback; all his forces were captured.
translations.idiomatic: As battle joined, Han was already in his camp setting fires; the army collapsed, Xunniyan fled alone, and the whole host was taken.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延父子世雄漠北，又先得玉璽三紐，自言為天所相，每自誇大。

translations.literal: Father and son had been heroes of the northern desert and had earlier obtained a jade seal with three knobs, saying Heaven supported them; they always boasted greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son had lorded over the northern desert and boasted of a triple-knobbed jade seal as Heaven's sign.

sentences.zh: 及此敗也，乃卑辭厚幣，遣使朝貢於昭帝，帝嘉之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: After this defeat he used humble words and rich gifts, sent envoys to court with tribute to Emperor Zhao, who commended him and gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: After this defeat he sent humble tribute to Emperor Zhao, who praised him and gave him an imperial daughter.

sentences.zh: 遜昵延死，子乞得龜立。

translations.literal: When Xunniyan died, his son Qidegui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunniyan died his son Qidegui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 復伐慕容廆，廆拒之。

translations.literal: He again attacked Murong Hui; Hui resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Murong Hui again; Hui met him in the field.

sentences.zh: 惠帝三年，乞得龜屯保澆水，固壘不戰，遣其兄悉跋堆襲廆子仁于柏林。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Hui, Qidegui encamped at Jiaoshui and held his fortresses without fighting; he sent his elder brother Xibadui to strike Hui's son Ren at Bolin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Hui, Qidegui camped on the Jiaoshui and refused battle, sending his brother Xibadui against Hui's son Ren at Bolin.

sentences.zh: 仁逆擊，斬悉跋堆。

translations.literal: Ren met the attack and beheaded Xibadui.
translations.idiomatic: Ren met him and beheaded Xibadui.

sentences.zh: 廆又攻乞得龜克之，乞得龜單騎夜奔，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: Hui again attacked Qidegui and defeated him; Qidegui fled alone by night on horseback; all his masses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Hui attacked again, broke him, and Qidegui fled alone by night while his army was taken.

sentences.zh: 乘勝長驅，入其固城，收資財億計，徙部人數萬戶以歸。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in long pursuit, he entered their stronghold city, seized wealth beyond counting, and moved tens of thousands of households of the tribe back.
translations.idiomatic: Hui drove into their stronghold, seized untold wealth, and moved tens of thousands of households away.

sentences.zh: 先是，海出大龜，枯死于平郭，至是而乞得龜敗。

translations.literal: Earlier the sea had cast up a great turtle that died dried on Pingguo; with this Qidegui was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: A great turtle had earlier washed ashore and died at Pingguo—an omen fulfilled in Qidegui's fall.

sentences.zh: 別部人逸豆歸殺乞得龜而自立，與慕容晃迭相攻擊。

translations.literal: A man of a separate division, Yidougui, killed Qidegui and set himself up, alternating attacks with Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui of a splinter line killed Qidegui and fought Murong Huang in turn.

sentences.zh: 遣其國相莫渾伐晃，而莫渾荒酒縱獵，為晃所破，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: He sent his state minister Mohun to attack Huang; Mohun indulged in wine and hunting and was defeated by Huang; more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his minister Mohun against Huang; Mohun drank and hunted and lost more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 建國八年，晃伐逸豆歸，逸豆歸拒之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jian'guo, Huang campaigned against Yidougui; Yidougui resisted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jian'guo, Huang marched against Yidougui, who resisted.

sentences.zh: 為晃所敗，殺其驍將涉亦幹。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Huang and his fierce general Sheyigan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang defeated him and slew his champion Sheyigan.

sentences.zh: 逸豆歸遠遁漠北，遂奔高麗。

translations.literal: Yidougui fled far into the northern desert and then fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui fled to the far north, then to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 晃徙其部眾五千餘落于昌黎，自是散滅矣。

translations.literal: Huang moved more than five thousand of his tribes to Changli; from this they were scattered and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang resettled five thousand of his households in Changli; the Yuwen were scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 徒何段就六眷，出於遼西。

translations.literal: Duan Jiuliujuan of the Tuge came from Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiuliujuan of the Tuge came from Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 其伯祖日陸眷，因亂被賣為漁陽烏丸大人庫辱官家奴。

translations.literal: His great-uncle Rilujuan, because of disorder, was sold as a slave to the Wuhuan great chief Kuruguan's household.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle Rilujuan, in troubled times, was sold as a slave to the Wuhuan chief Kuruguan.

sentences.zh: 諸大人集會幽州，皆持唾壺，唯庫辱官獨無，乃唾日陸眷口中。

translations.literal: When the great chiefs assembled in Youzhou all held spittoons; only Kuruguan had none, and he spat into Rilujuan's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When chiefs met in Youzhou each had a spittoon; Kuruguan alone had none and spat into Rilujuan's mouth.

sentences.zh: 日陸眷因咽之，西向拜天曰：「願使主君之智慧祿相，盡移入我腹中。」

translations.literal: Rilujuan swallowed it, bowed west to Heaven and said: "May my lord's wisdom, fortune, and rank all pass into my belly."
translations.idiomatic: Rilujuan swallowed and prayed westward, "May my master's wisdom and fortune pass into me."

sentences.zh: 其後漁陽大饑。

translations.literal: Afterward Yuyang suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuyang suffered famine.

sentences.zh: 庫辱官以日陸眷為健，使將人詣遼西逐食，詔誘亡叛，遂至強盛。

translations.literal: Kuruguan, because Rilujuan was strong, had him lead men to Liaoxi to seek food; he summoned and enticed fugitives and thereupon grew powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Kuruguan sent the able Rilujuan to Liaoxi for food; he gathered fugitives and grew mighty.

sentences.zh: 日陸眷死，弟乞珍代立。

translations.literal: When Rilujuan died, his younger brother Qizhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Rilujuan died his brother Qizhen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乞珍死，子務目塵代立，即就六眷父也。

translations.literal: When Qizhen died, his son Wumuchen succeeded—Jiuliujuan's father.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhen's son Wumuchen succeeded—the father of Jiuliujuan.

sentences.zh: 據遼西之地而臣于晉。

translations.literal: He held the lands of Liaoxi and submitted to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He held Liaoxi and submitted to Jin.

sentences.zh: 其所統三萬餘家，控弦上馬四五萬騎。

translations.literal: He ruled more than thirty thousand households, with forty to fifty thousand horse under bow.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled thirty thousand households and forty to fifty thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 穆帝時，幽州刺史王浚以段氏數為己用，深德之，乃表封務目塵為遼西公，假大單于印綬。

translations.literal: During Emperor Mu's reign, Youzhou Inspector Wang Jun, because the Duan clan had repeatedly served him, was deeply grateful and memorialized to enfeoff Wumuchen as Duke of Liaoxi and grant the great Shanyu seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu, Wang Jun of Youzhou, indebted to the Duan, had Wumuchen enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi with the great Shanyu seal.

sentences.zh: 浚使務目塵率萬餘騎伐石勒于常山封龍山下，大破之。

translations.literal: Jun had Wumuchen lead more than ten thousand horse to attack Shi Le at Fenglongshan in Changshan and routed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Wumuchen with ten thousand horse against Shi Le at Fenglongshan and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 務目塵死，就六眷立。

translations.literal: When Wumuchen died, Jiuliujuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wumuchen died, Jiuliujuan took his place.

sentences.zh: 就六眷與弟疋磾、從弟末波等率五萬餘騎圍石勒于襄國。

translations.literal: Jiuliujuan with his younger brother Pidi and cousin Mobo led more than fifty thousand horse to surround Shi Le at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuliujuan, his brother Pidi, and cousin Mobo besieged Shi Le at Xiangguo with fifty thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 勒登城望之，見將士皆釋伏寢臥，無警備之意。

translations.literal: Le ascended the wall and looked at them; he saw officers and soldiers all lying down asleep with no sign of alert.
translations.idiomatic: Le climbed the wall and saw the besiegers sleeping without guard.

sentences.zh: 勒因其懈怠，選募勇健，穿城突出，直沖末波，生禽之。

translations.literal: Le took advantage of their slackness, chose brave men, broke out through the wall, and charged straight at Mobo, capturing him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Le chose brave men, burst out, and seized Mobo alive.

sentences.zh: 置之座上，與飲宴盡歡，約為父子，盟誓而遣之。

translations.literal: He placed him on a seat, drank and feasted together to the full, made a pact as father and son, swore an oath, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He seated Mobo, feasted with him, swore brotherhood, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 末波既得免，就六眷等遂攝軍而還，不復報浚，歸於遼西。

translations.literal: Mobo having escaped, Jiuliujuan and the others thereupon withdrew their army and returned, no longer reporting to Jun, and went back to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo freed, the Duan withdrew without reporting to Jun and returned to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，末波常不敢南向溲焉。

translations.literal: From this onward Mobo never dared urinate facing south.
translations.idiomatic: After that Mobo never relieved himself facing south.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，末波曰：「吾父在南。」

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Mobo said: "My father is in the south."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "My father is in the south."

sentences.zh: 其感勒不害己也如此。

translations.literal: Such was his feeling for Le's sparing him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his gratitude that Le had spared him.

sentences.zh: 就六眷死，其子幼弱，疋磾與劉琨世子群奔喪。

translations.literal: When Jiuliujuan died his sons were young; Pidi went with Liu Kun's heir Qun to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuliujuan died his sons were infants; Pidi went with Liu Kun's heir Qun to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 疋磾陰卷甲而往，欲殺其叔羽鱗及末波而奪其國。

translations.literal: Pidi secretly rolled up armor and went, intending to kill his uncles Yulin and Mobo and seize the state.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi marched in secret armor intending to kill his uncles Yulin and Mobo and seize the tribe.

sentences.zh: 末波等知之，遣軍逆擊疋磾。

translations.literal: Mobo and the others learned of it and sent troops to intercept Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo learned of it and sent troops to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 劉群為末波所獲。

translations.literal: Liu Qun was captured by Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qun was taken by Mobo.

sentences.zh: 疋磾走還薊，懼琨禽己，請琨宴會，因執而害之。

translations.literal: Pidi fled back to Ji; fearing Kun would seize him, he invited Kun to a banquet and there seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi fled to Ji, then invited Kun to a feast and murdered him.

sentences.zh: 疋磾既殺劉琨，與羽鱗、末波自相攻擊，部眾乖離。

translations.literal: After Pidi killed Liu Kun he and Yulin and Mobo attacked one another; the tribes split apart.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Kun he warred with Yulin and Mobo until the tribe split.

sentences.zh: 欲擁其眾徙保上穀，阻軍都之險，以距末波等。

translations.literal: He wished to lead his masses to move and hold Shanggu, using the danger of Jundu Pass to resist Mobo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to move his people to Shanggu and hold Jundu Pass against Mobo.

sentences.zh: 平文帝聞之，陰嚴精騎，將擊之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Pingwen heard of this, he secretly mustered picked cavalry to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Emperor Pingwen quietly assembled elite horsemen to attack him.

sentences.zh: 疋磾恐懼，南奔樂陵。

translations.literal: Pidi was afraid and fled south to Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Pidi fled south to Leling.

sentences.zh: 後石勒遣石季龍擊段文鴦于樂陵，破之，生禽文鴦。

translations.literal: Later Shi Le sent Shi Jilong to attack Duan Wenyang at Leling, defeated him, and captured Wenyang alive.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Le sent Shi Jilong against Duan Wenyang at Leling, broke his force, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 疋磾遂率其屬及諸塢壁降于石勒。

translations.literal: Pidi thereupon led his followers and the various fortified hamlets to surrender to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi then led his kin and the walled settlements to submit to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 末波自稱幽州刺史，屯遼西。

translations.literal: Mobo called himself Inspector of Youzhou and stationed himself in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo styled himself Inspector of Youzhou and garrisoned Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 末波死，國人因立陸眷弟護遼為主。

translations.literal: When Mobo died, the people of the state then established Lujuan's younger brother Huliao as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: After Mobo died, the people installed Lujuan's younger brother Huliao as ruler.

sentences.zh: 烈帝時，假護遼驃騎大將軍、幽州刺史、大單于、北平公，弟郁蘭撫軍將軍、冀州刺史、勃海公。

translations.literal: In Emperor Lie's time, Huliao was provisionally granted the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Inspector of Youzhou, Great Chanyu, and Duke of Beiping, and his younger brother Yulan was made General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Jizhou, and Duke of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Lie's time, Huliao was provisionally granted the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Inspector of Youzhou, Great Chanyu, and Duke of Beiping, while his younger brother Yulan received the titles General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Jizhou, and Duke of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 建國元年，石季龍征護遼於遼西，護遼奔于平岡山，遂投慕容晃，晃殺之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianguo, Shi Jilong campaigned against Huliao in Liaoxi; Huliao fled to Mount Pinggang and then submitted to Murong Huang, who killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianguo, Shi Jilong campaigned against Huliao in Liaoxi. Huliao fled to Mount Pinggang and then threw himself on Murong Huang, who killed him.

sentences.zh: 郁蘭奔石季龍，以所徙鮮卑五千人配之，使屯令支。

translations.literal: Yulan fled to Shi Jilong, who assigned to him five thousand Xianbei who had been relocated and made him garrison Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yulan fled to Shi Jilong, who assigned him five thousand relocated Xianbei and ordered him to garrison Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 郁蘭死，子龕代之。

translations.literal: When Yulan died, his son Kan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulan died, his son Kan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 及冉閔之亂，龕率眾南移，遂據齊地。

translations.literal: When Ran Min's turmoil came, Kan led his people south and then occupied the land of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: During Ran Min's upheaval, Kan led his people south and occupied the Qi region.

sentences.zh: 慕容俊使弟玄恭率眾伐龕於廣固，執龕送之薊。

translations.literal: Murong Jun sent his younger brother Xuangong to lead troops and attack Kan at Guanggu; he seized Kan and sent him to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent his younger brother Xuangong to lead troops against Kan at Guanggu. Xuangong captured Kan and sent him to Ji.

sentences.zh: 俊毒其目而殺之，坑其徒三千餘人。

translations.literal: Jun poisoned his eyes and killed him, and buried alive more than three thousand of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Jun poisoned his eyes and killed him, then buried alive more than three thousand of his followers.

sentences.zh: 高車，蓋古赤狄之餘種也。

translations.literal: The Gaoche were the remnant stock of the ancient Red Di.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche were descendants of the ancient Red Di.

sentences.zh: 初號為狄曆，北方以為高車、丁零。

translations.literal: At first they were called Dili; northerners regarded them as Gaoche and Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: They were first known as the Dili; northerners called them the Gaoche or Dingling.

sentences.zh: 其語略與匈奴同而時有小異。

translations.literal: Their speech broadly matched that of the Xiongnu, with occasional small differences.
translations.idiomatic: Their language was largely like the Xiongnu tongue, with minor variations.

sentences.zh: 或云：其先匈奴甥也。

translations.literal: Some say their forebears were nephews of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that they sprang from Xiongnu kin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 其種有狄氏、袁紇氏、斛律氏、解批氏、護骨氏、異奇斤氏。

translations.literal: Their clans included the Di, Yuanhe, Hulü, Jiepi, Hugu, and Yiqijin lines.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes included the Di, Yuanhe, Hulü, Jiepi, Hugu, and Yiqijin.

sentences.zh: 俗云：匈奴單于生二女，姿容甚美，國人皆以為神。

translations.literal: Custom holds that the Xiongnu chanyu fathered two daughters of surpassing beauty, and the people all regarded them as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Legend says the Xiongnu chanyu had two daughters of rare beauty whom the people revered as divine.

sentences.zh: 單于曰：「吾有此女，安可配人？

translations.literal: The chanyu said: "I have these daughters—how could I give them to any man?
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu said, "These daughters of mine cannot be wed to mortal men.

sentences.zh: 將以與天。」

translations.literal: I shall give them to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I will offer them to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 乃于國北無人之地築高臺，置二女其上曰：「請天自迎之。」

translations.literal: He then built a high terrace in an uninhabited place north of the realm, set the two daughters upon it, and said: "Let Heaven come and receive them itself."
translations.idiomatic: He built a high platform in empty country north of his realm, placed the girls upon it, and prayed, "Let Heaven come and take them."

sentences.zh: 經三年，其母欲迎之。

translations.literal: After three years their mother wished to bring them back.
translations.idiomatic: After three years their mother wished to fetch them home.

sentences.zh: 單于曰：「不可，未徹之間耳。」

translations.literal: The chanyu said: "It cannot be done—not until the offering is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu refused: "No—the rite is not yet finished."

sentences.zh: 復一年，乃有一老狼，晝夜守台嗥呼，因穿台下為空穴，經時不去。

translations.literal: Another year passed, and an old wolf came, guarding the terrace day and night and howling; it dug a hole beneath the platform and for a long time would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Another year on, an old wolf kept the platform day and night, howling and burrowing beneath it without departing.

sentences.zh: 其小女曰：「吾父處我于此，欲以與天，而今狼來，或是神物，無使之然。」

translations.literal: The younger daughter said: "Our father placed us here to give us to Heaven; now a wolf has come—perhaps it is a spirit; do not thwart it."
