translations.idiomatic: The younger daughter said, "Father set us here for Heaven; if this wolf is a divine being, we must not resist."

sentences.zh: 將下就之。

translations.literal: She was about to go down to it.
translations.idiomatic: She prepared to go down to the wolf.

sentences.zh: 其姊夫驚曰：「此是畜生，無乃辱父母？」

translations.literal: Her elder sister was alarmed and said: "That is a beast—will we not shame our parents?"
translations.idiomatic: Her sister cried out, "It is only an animal—would that not disgrace our parents?"

sentences.zh: 妹不從，下為狼妻而產子。

translations.literal: The younger sister would not listen; she went down, became the wolf's wife, and bore children.
translations.idiomatic: The girl disobeyed, went down, wed the wolf, and bore his young.

sentences.zh: 後遂滋繁成國。

translations.literal: Afterward they multiplied and became a state.
translations.idiomatic: Their line multiplied until it formed a people.

sentences.zh: 故其人好引聲長歌，又似狼嗥。

translations.literal: Hence these people love to draw out their voices in long songs that also resemble wolves' howls.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason they favor long, drawn-out songs that sound like wolves howling.

sentences.zh: 無都統大帥，當種各有君長。

translations.literal: They had no paramount commander; each tribe had its own chief.
translations.idiomatic: They had no single overlord—each branch kept its own leader.

sentences.zh: 為性粗猛，黨類同心，至於寇難，翕然相依。

translations.literal: By nature they were rough and fierce; within a faction they stood as one heart, and in raids they relied on one another at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and unruly by nature, they stood together in a crisis and backed one another in raids.

sentences.zh: 鬥無行陣，頭別衝突，乍出乍入，不能堅戰。

translations.literal: In battle they formed no ranks; each man charged on his own, darting in and out, unable to stand firm in prolonged fighting.
translations.idiomatic: They fought without formation, each warrior charging alone in sudden rushes, and could not sustain a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 其俗，蹲踞褻黷，無所忌避。

translations.literal: In their customs they squatted casually and were unrestrained, without taboo.
translations.idiomatic: They squatted informally in daily life and observed few proprieties.

sentences.zh: 婚姻用牛馬納聘以為榮，結言既定，男党營車闌馬，令女黨恣取上馬，袒乘出闌，馬主立闌外，振手驚馬，不墜者即取之，墜則更取，數滿乃止。

translations.literal: In marriage, offering cattle and horses as bride-price was deemed honorable; once the pledge was fixed, the men's side set up a corral of carts and horses and let the women's side take horses at will and mount bare-backed to ride out; the horse's owner stood outside the corral and startled the horse with a wave—whoever did not fall took the horse; if one fell, another was taken, until the allotted number was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage honor lay in bride-wealth of cattle and horses; when the match was set, the groom's kin penned horses in a ring while the bride's kin mounted bareback and rode out; owners outside startled each mount—whoever stayed seated kept the horse, and the ritual continued until the required number was won.

sentences.zh: 俗無穀，不作酒。

translations.literal: By custom they had no grain and made no wine.
translations.idiomatic: They ate no grain by custom and brewed no wine.

sentences.zh: 迎婦之日，男女相將，振馬酪熟肉節解。

translations.literal: On the day the bride was welcomed, men and women went together, shaking mare's milk and cooked meat in festive portions.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding day men and women went together, sharing fermented mare's milk and boiled meat in celebration.

sentences.zh: 主人延賓，亦無行位，穹廬前叢坐，飲宴終日，復留其宿。

translations.literal: When the host received guests there were also no places by rank; they sat in a cluster before the yurt and feasted all day, then kept guests overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Hosts entertained guests without order of seat, drinking all day in a circle before the tent and lodging them overnight.

sentences.zh: 明日，將婦歸。

translations.literal: The next day they took the bride home.
translations.idiomatic: On the morrow the bride was brought to her new home.

sentences.zh: 既而夫黨還入其家馬群，極取良馬，父母弟兄雖惜，終無言者。

translations.literal: Then the husband's kin entered her family's herd and took the finest horses; though parents and brothers regretted the loss, in the end they said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The groom's kin then entered the bride's herd and took the best horses; parents and brothers grieved but held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 頗諱取寡婦，而優憐之。

translations.literal: They rather shrank from taking widows, yet treated them with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: They shunned marrying widows yet showed them unusual kindness.

sentences.zh: 其畜產自有記識，雖闌縱在野，終無妄取。

translations.literal: Their livestock bore their own marks; though animals ranged loose in the wild, none were taken wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Every beast was marked; even on the open steppe none was stolen by mistake.

sentences.zh: 俗不清潔，喜致震霆。

translations.literal: By custom they were not fastidious and delighted in provoking thunder.
translations.idiomatic: They cared little for cleanliness and dreaded thunder.

sentences.zh: 每震，則叫呼射天而棄之移去。

translations.literal: Whenever it thundered they shouted and shot toward heaven, then abandoned that place and moved away.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder struck they cried out, shot arrows at the sky, and moved camp.

sentences.zh: 來歲秋，馬肥，復相率候於震所，埋羖羊，燃火拔刀，女巫祝說，似如中國祓除，而群隊馳馬旋繞，百匝乃止。

translations.literal: In autumn of the following year, when horses were fat, they again gathered at the place of the thunder, buried a ram, lit a fire, drew knives, and the shamaness prayed—much like Chinese purification rites—while the host galloped in circles around the site a hundred times before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Next autumn, when the herds were fat, they returned to the thunder site, buried a ram, kindled fire, and with knives drawn let a shamaness pray as in Chinese exorcism while riders circled a hundred times on horseback.

sentences.zh: 人持一束柳桋回，豎之，以乳酪灌焉。

translations.literal: Each person carried home a bundle of willow wands, set them upright, and poured mare's milk over them.
translations.idiomatic: Each man took willow branches home, planted them upright, and poured mare's milk upon them.

sentences.zh: 婦人以皮裹羊骸，戴之首上，縈屈髮鬢而綴之，有似軒冕。

translations.literal: Women wrapped sheep bones in hide, wore them on their heads, coiled and pinned their hair around them so that it resembled a court cap.
translations.idiomatic: Women bound sheep bones in hide, wore them on the head, and coiled their hair about them like a ceremonial crown.

sentences.zh: 其死亡葬送，掘地作坎，坐屍于中，張臂引弓，佩刀挾槊，無異於生，而露坎不掩。

translations.literal: For the dead they dug a pit, seated the corpse within with arms spread as if drawing a bow, knife at the belt and spear in the armpit, no different from life, and left the pit uncovered.
translations.idiomatic: They buried the dead in open pits, seating the corpse with bow arm extended, knife belted and spear at the side as in life, without covering the grave.

sentences.zh: 時有震死及疫癘，則為之祈福；

translations.literal: When people died by lightning or pestilence they performed rites to seek blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Death by lightning or plague called for blessing rites;

sentences.zh: 若安全無他，則為報賽。

translations.literal: if all was safe and nothing else befell them, they offered thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: when fortune held, they offered thanksgiving sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 多殺雜畜，燒骨以燎，走馬繞旋，多者數百匝。

translations.literal: They slaughtered many mixed beasts, burned the bones for flame, and galloped circling—sometimes hundreds of rounds.
translations.idiomatic: They killed many animals, burned the bones as offering, and galloped in circles—sometimes hundreds of times.

sentences.zh: 男女無小大，皆集會。

translations.literal: Men and women, young and old, all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old of both sexes gathered together.

sentences.zh: 平吉之人，則歌舞作樂；

translations.literal: In peaceful times they sang and made music;
translations.idiomatic: In good fortune they sang and danced;

sentences.zh: 死喪之家，則悲吟哭泣。

translations.literal: in houses of mourning they mourned in chanted weeping.
translations.idiomatic: in mourning they wailed in lament.

sentences.zh: 其遷徙隨水草，衣皮食肉，牛、羊畜產，盡與蠕蠕同。

translations.literal: They moved with water and grass, wore hides and ate meat; cattle, sheep, and herds were all the same as the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: They followed pasture and water, dressed in hides and lived on meat; their herds matched the Rouran in every way.

sentences.zh: 唯車輪高大，輻數至多。

translations.literal: Only their cart wheels were tall and their spokes exceedingly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Only their cart wheels were unusually high, with many spokes.

sentences.zh: 徙于鹿渾海西北百餘里，部落強大，常與蠕蠕為敵，亦每侵盜于魏。

translations.literal: They moved to a place more than a hundred li northwest of the Luhun Sea; their tribes grew strong, they were often enemies of the Rouran, and they also raided Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They settled northwest of the Luhun Sea; as their tribes grew mighty they fought the Rouran and raided Wei as well.

sentences.zh: 魏道武襲之，大破其諸部。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu of Wei attacked them and greatly defeated their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu struck them and shattered their confederacies.

sentences.zh: 後道武復度弱洛水，西行至鹿渾海，停駕簡輕騎，西北行百餘里，襲破之，虜獲生口、牛馬羊二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Later Daowu again crossed the Ruoluo River, marched west to the Luhun Sea, halted and selected light cavalry, and going northwest more than a hundred li struck and broke them, capturing people and more than two hundred thousand head of cattle, horses, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu later crossed the Ruoluo, reached the Luhun Sea, chose light horse, and riding northwest over a hundred li smashed them, taking captives and more than two hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 復討其餘種於狼山，大破之。

translations.literal: He again attacked their remaining clans at Langshan and defeated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the remnant clans at Langshan and broke them again.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，分命諸將為東西二道，道武親勒六軍從中道，自駁髯水西北，徇略其部，諸軍同時雲合，破其雜種三十餘落。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage toured the north; he ordered generals into eastern and western columns while Daowu himself led the six armies on the center road from Boyan Water northwest, sweeping their tribes; the armies converged at once and broke more than thirty scattered encampments.
translations.idiomatic: On a northern tour Daowu split his generals east and west while he led the main host from Boyan Water northwest, and the columns united to crush more than thirty Gaoche settlements.

sentences.zh: 衛王儀別督諸將從西北絕漠千餘里，復破其遺迸七部。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Wei separately commanded the generals northwest across more than a thousand li of desert and again broke seven fleeing divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Wei took another column more than a thousand li across the desert and destroyed seven fleeing bands.

sentences.zh: 於是高車大懼，諸部震駭。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Gaoche were greatly afraid and all tribes were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche were terrified and every tribe trembled.

sentences.zh: 道武自牛川南引，大校獵，以高車為圍，騎徒遮列，周七百餘里，聚雜獸於其中，因驅至平城，即以高車眾起鹿苑，南因台陰，北距長城，東包白登，屬之西山。

translations.literal: Daowu led south from Niuchuan, held a great hunt, used the Gaoche as a living fence, and with horsemen posted in a cordon for more than seven hundred li drove mixed game within it, then drove them to Pingcheng; with the Gaoche multitude he raised a deer park south along the terrace shade, north against the Long Wall, east enclosing Baideng, reaching the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Niuchuan southward, Daowu held a grand hunt, ringed seven hundred li with Gaoche horsemen as a living fence, drove game within, and brought it to Pingcheng, where he made a royal park bounded by the terrace, the Long Wall, Baideng, and the western hills.

sentences.zh: 尋而高車侄利曷莫弗敕力犍率其九百餘落內附，拜敕力犍為揚威將軍，置司馬、參軍，賜谷二萬斛。

translations.literal: Before long the Gaoche Zhilihemofu Chilijian led more than nine hundred encampments to submit inward; Chilijian was appointed General Who Displays Might, with staff officers and aides, and granted twenty thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Gaoche chief Chilijian brought nine hundred settlements to submit and was made General Who Displays Might with staff and twenty thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 後高車解批莫弗幡豆建復率其部三十餘落內附，亦拜為威遠將軍，置司馬、參軍，賜衣服，歲給廩食。

translations.literal: Later the Gaoche Jiepihemofu Fandoujian again led more than thirty of his encampments to submit; he too was made General of Far Might, given staff officers, clothing, and yearly grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fandoujian of the Jiepi line led thirty settlements inward and received the title General of Far Might, staff, robes, and annual grain.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕社侖破敗之後，收拾部落，轉徙廣漠之北，侵入高車之地。

translations.literal: After Shelun of the Rouran was defeated he gathered his tribes, moved to the far north of the desert, and invaded Gaoche lands.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat Shelun of the Rouran regathered his people, shifted deep into the northern desert, and encroached on Gaoche territory.

sentences.zh: 斛律部帥倍侯利患之，曰：「新侖新集，兵貧馬少，易與耳！」

translations.literal: Beihouli, chief of the Hulü tribe, resented this and said: "The new Shelun has only just assembled—his soldiers are few and horses poor; he will be easy to handle!"
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli, chief of the Hulü, said, "Shelun is newly gathered—few men and poor horses; we can crush him!"

sentences.zh: 乃舉眾掩擊，入其國落。

translations.literal: He then raised his host in a surprise attack and entered Shelun's encampments.
translations.idiomatic: He struck by surprise and overran Shelun's camps.

sentences.zh: 高車昧利，不顧後患，分其廬室，妻其婦女，安息寢臥不起。

translations.literal: The Gaoche, blinded by gain, gave no thought to later trouble; they divided Shelun's dwellings, took his women, and rested in sleep without rising.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche, greedy for plunder, ignored the aftermath, seized Shelun's tents and wives, and slept at ease.

sentences.zh: 社侖登高望見，乃招集亡散得千人，晨振殺之，走而脫者十二三。

translations.literal: Shelun climbed high, looked out, gathered a thousand scattered men, struck at dawn, and killed them; only twelve or thirteen in ten escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun watched from a height, rallied a thousand fugitives, attacked at dawn, and routed them—only one or two in ten escaped.

sentences.zh: 倍侯利遂奔魏，賜爵孟都公。

translations.literal: Beihouli then fled to Wei and was enfeoffed as Duke of Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli fled to Wei and was created Duke of Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 侯利質直，勇健過人，奮戈陷陣，有異於眾。

translations.literal: Beihouli was upright by nature and surpassingly brave; charging with spear he broke formations unlike the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Beihouli was plain and surpassingly brave, breaking ranks with his spear like no other.

sentences.zh: 北方人善用五十蓍筮吉凶，每中，故得親幸，賞賜豐厚，命其少子曷堂內侍。

translations.literal: Northerners were skilled at divining fortune and misfortune with fifty yarrow stalks, and he always hit the mark; therefore he won close favor, rich rewards, and his youngest son Yetang was ordered to attend within.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners divined with fifty yarrow stalks, and he was never wrong; favored and richly rewarded, he had his son Yetang serve at court.

sentences.zh: 及倍侯利卒，道武悼惜，葬以魏禮，諡曰忠壯王。

translations.literal: When Beihouli died, Daowu mourned him, buried him by Wei rites, and gave the posthumous title Loyal and Valiant King.
translations.idiomatic: At Beihouli's death Daowu mourned him, buried him with Wei ceremony, and titled him Loyal and Valiant King.

sentences.zh: 後詔將軍伊謂帥二萬騎北襲高車余種袁紇烏，頻破之。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered General Yiwei to lead twenty thousand horse north to strike the Gaoche remnant Yuanhe clans and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later General Yiwei was sent with twenty thousand horse to strike the Yuanhe remnant of the Gaoche and defeated them again and again.

sentences.zh: 道武時，分散諸部，唯高車以類粗獷，不任使役，故得別為部落。

translations.literal: In Daowu's time the tribes were dispersed; only the Gaoche, because their kind was coarse and wild and unfit for corvée, were allowed to remain a separate people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daowu the tribes were broken up; only the Gaoche, deemed too rough for labor service, were left as a distinct people.

sentences.zh: 後太武征蠕蠕，破之而還。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Rouran, defeated them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Rouran, broke them, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 至漠南，聞高車東部在巳尼陂，人畜甚眾，去官軍千餘里，將遣左僕射安原等討之。

translations.literal: Reaching the south of the desert he heard that the eastern Gaoche were encamped at Shinipo with vast herds and people, more than a thousand li from the army; he was about to send Left Vice-Director Anyuan and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: South of the desert he learned that eastern Gaoche held Shinipo with huge herds a thousand li away and prepared to send Anyuan and others against them.

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫翰、尚書令劉潔等諫，太武不聽。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Changsun Han and Director of the Department Liu Jie remonstrated, but Taiwu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Han and Liu Jie advised against it, but Taiwu refused to heed them.

sentences.zh: 乃遣原等併發新附高車合萬騎，至於巳尼陂，高車諸部望軍而降者數十萬落，獲馬牛羊亦百餘萬，皆徙置漠南千里之地。

translations.literal: He then sent Anyuan and others together with newly submitted Gaoche to the number of ten thousand horse; reaching Shinipo, several hundred thousand Gaoche encampments surrendered at sight of the army; they also took more than a million horses, cattle, and sheep, and all were moved to settle a thousand li south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Anyuan marched with ten thousand horse including newly submitted Gaoche; at Shinipo hundreds of thousands of encampments surrendered and more than a million head were taken and resettled south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 乘高車，逐水草，畜牧蕃息，數年之後，漸知粒食，歲致獻貢。

translations.literal: Riding their high carts they followed water and grass; their herds multiplied, and after several years they gradually learned grain food and sent tribute each year.
translations.idiomatic: They followed pasture in their high carts, their herds flourished, and within years they learned grain and paid yearly tribute.

sentences.zh: 由是國家馬及牛、羊遂至於賤，氈皮委積。

translations.literal: From this the state's horses and cattle and sheep became so plentiful as to be cheap, and felts and hides piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter imperial horses, cattle, and sheep grew abundant and cheap, and felts and hides heaped high.

sentences.zh: 文成時，五部高車合聚祭天，眾至數萬，大會走馬，殺牲遊繞，歌吟忻忻。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wencheng the five Gaoche divisions gathered to sacrifice to Heaven; the assembly reached tens of thousands; they held a great horse race, slaughtered beasts, circled in sport, and sang in glad voices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng the five Gaoche divisions met to worship Heaven—tens of thousands strong—with horse races, sacrifice, circling sport, and joyful song.

sentences.zh: 其俗稱自前世以來，無盛於此會。

translations.literal: In their custom they said that since former ages there had been no assembly greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: By their reckoning no gathering in memory had ever matched it.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨幸，莫不忻悅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage came in person, none were not glad.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor attended in person, all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 後孝文召高車之眾，隨車賀南討，高車不願南行，遂推袁紇樹者為主，相率北叛，游踐金陵。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowen summoned the Gaoche to follow the army in congratulating the southern campaign; the Gaoche did not wish to march south, so they made Yuanhe Shuzhe their leader, rose in rebellion together northward, and ranged through Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaowen called the Gaoche to join his southern campaign; refusing to go south, they made Yuanhe Shuzhe chief, rebelled north in a body, and raided about Jinling.

sentences.zh: 都督宇文福追討，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Supervisor-in-Chief Yuwen Fu pursued and attacked; he was greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Fu pursued them, suffered a heavy defeat, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又詔平北將軍、江陽王繼為都督討之。

translations.literal: An edict again appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Prince of Jiangyang Ji, as commander to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The court again named Prince Ji of Jiangyang, General Who Pacifies the North, to command the campaign.

sentences.zh: 繼先遣人慰勞樹者。

translations.literal: Ji first sent men to console Shuzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ji first sent envoys to reassure Shuzhe.

sentences.zh: 樹者入蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Shuzhe entered the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhe fled among the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 尋悔，相率而降。

translations.literal: Soon he repented and led his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it and surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 高車之族又有十二姓：一曰泣伏利氏，二曰吐盧氏，三曰乙旃氏，四曰大連氏，五曰窟賀氏，六曰達薄氏，七曰阿侖氏，八曰莫允氏，九曰俟分氏，十曰副伏羅氏，十一曰乞袁氏，十二曰右叔沛氏。

translations.literal: Among the Gaoche there were also twelve surnames: first the Qifuli, second the Tulü, third the Yizhan, fourth the Dalian, fifth the Kugu, sixth the Dabo, seventh the Alun, eighth the Moyun, ninth the Houfen, tenth the Fufuluo, eleventh the Qiyuan, and twelfth the Youshupei.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche also counted twelve clans: Qifuli, Tulü, Yizhan, Dalian, Kugu, Dabo, Alun, Moyun, Houfen, Fufuluo, Qiyuan, and Youshupei.

sentences.zh: 先是，副伏羅部為蠕蠕所役屬。

translations.literal: Earlier the Fufuluo division had been subject to and serving the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Fufuluo had been vassals of the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 豆侖之世，蠕蠕亂離，國部分散，副伏羅阿伏至羅與從弟窮奇俱統領高車之眾十餘萬落。

translations.literal: In the time of Doulun the Rouran fell into disorder and the realm split apart; Afozheluo of the Fufuluo and his cousin Qiongqi together commanded more than a hundred thousand Gaoche encampments.
translations.idiomatic: When Doulun ruled, Rouran disorder split the realm; Afozheluo and his cousin Qiongqi led more than a hundred thousand Gaoche tents.

sentences.zh: 太和十一年，豆侖犯塞，阿伏至羅等固諫不從，怒率所部之眾西叛，至前部西北，自立為王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe, Doulun raided the frontier; Afozheluo and others firmly remonstrated but were not obeyed; in anger they led their followers west in rebellion to the northwest of the Former Qian and set themselves up as kings.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year eleven Doulun raided the border; Afozheluo urged restraint in vain, then led his people west beyond the Former Qian and proclaimed kingship.

sentences.zh: 國人號之曰候婁匐勒，猶魏言大天子也；

translations.literal: The people called him Hou Lou Fule, as Wei speech has it "great Son of Heaven";
translations.idiomatic: His people titled him Hou Lou Fule—"great Son of Heaven" in Wei parlance;

sentences.zh: 窮奇號候倍，猶魏言儲主也。

translations.literal: Qiongqi was called Hou Bei, as Wei speech has it "heir lord."
translations.idiomatic: Qiongqi was called Hou Bei—"heir lord" in Wei speech.

sentences.zh: 二人和穆，分部而立，阿伏至羅居北，窮奇在南。

translations.literal: The two were harmonious and divided to rule—Afozheluo in the north, Qiongqi in the south.
translations.idiomatic: They ruled in amity, Afozheluo in the north and Qiongqi in the south.

sentences.zh: 豆侖追討之，頻為阿伏至羅所敗，乃引眾東徙。

translations.literal: Doulun pursued and attacked them but was repeatedly defeated by Afozheluo and then led his masses eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Doulun pursued, was beaten again and again, and finally moved his host east.

sentences.zh: 十四年，阿伏至羅遣商胡越者至京師，以二箭奉貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Afozheluo sent the merchant Yuezhe to the capital to present tribute of two arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen Afozheluo sent the trader Yuezhe to court with two arrows as tribute.

sentences.zh: 云：「蠕蠕為天子之賊，臣諫之不從，遂叛來此，而自豎立，當為天子討除蠕蠕。」

translations.literal: He said: "The Rouran are the Son of Heaven's enemies; I remonstrated and was not obeyed, so I rebelled and came here, setting myself up to destroy the Rouran on the Son of Heaven's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: He declared, "The Rouran are the emperor's foes; when I warned Doulun in vain I came west and set myself up to fight them for the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 孝文未之信也，遣使者于提往觀虛實。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen did not yet believe him and sent the envoy Yuti to observe the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen doubted him and sent Yuti to learn the facts.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅與窮奇遣使者薄頡隨提來朝，貢其方物。

translations.literal: Afozheluo and Qiongqi sent the envoy Boie to accompany Yuti to court and present their local products.
translations.idiomatic: Afozheluo and Qiongqi sent Boie with Yuti to court with regional gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔員外散騎侍郎可足渾長生復與于提使高車，各賜繡褲褶一具，雜彩百匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Supernumerary Gentleman Kehun Changsheng to go again with Yuti as envoys to the Gaoche; each was granted one set of embroidered trousers and jacket and a hundred bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Changsheng with Yuti back to the Gaoche, each man receiving embroidered riding dress and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 窮奇後為嚈噠所殺，虜其子彌俄突等。

translations.literal: Later Qiongqi was killed by the Hephthalites, who captured his sons Mie'etuo and others.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Hephthalites killed Qiongqi and took his sons, including Mie'etuo.

sentences.zh: 其眾分散，或來奔附，或投蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Their followers scattered; some came to submit, some fled to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: His people scattered—some submitted to Wei, some to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 詔遣宣威將軍、羽林監孟威撫納降人，置之高平鎮。

translations.literal: An edict sent General Who Proclaims Might, Feathered-Forest Inspector Meng Wei, to comfort and settle those who surrendered and place them at Gaoping garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent General Meng Wei of the Feathered Forest to settle the refugees at Gaoping garrison.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅長子蒸阿伏至羅余妻，謀害阿伏至羅，阿伏至羅殺之。

translations.literal: Afozheluo's eldest son Zheng plotted against Afozheluo's surviving wife; Afozheluo killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Afozheluo's eldest son Zheng plotted against his stepmother, and Afozheluo executed him.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅又殘暴，大失眾心，眾共殺之，立其宗人跋利延為主。

translations.literal: Afozheluo was again cruel and greatly lost the hearts of the people; the masses together killed him and set up his clansman Baliyan as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Afozheluo grew tyrannical and lost his people, who slew him and raised his kinsman Baliyan.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，嚈噠伐高車，將納彌俄突。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Hephthalites attacked the Gaoche, intending to install Mie'etuo.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Hephthalites invaded the Gaoche to place Mie'etuo on the throne.

sentences.zh: 國人殺跋利延，迎彌俄突而立之。

translations.literal: The people killed Baliyan and welcomed Mie'etuo to set him up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes killed Baliyan and enthroned Mie'etuo.

sentences.zh: 彌俄突既立，復遣朝貢，又奉表獻金方一、銀方一、金杖二、馬七匹、駝十頭。

translations.literal: Once Mie'etuo was established he again sent court tribute and also submitted a memorial offering one gold ingot, one silver ingot, two gold staves, seven horses, and ten camels.
translations.idiomatic: Mie'etuo then sent tribute again, including gold and silver blocks, two gold staffs, seven horses, and ten camels.

sentences.zh: 詔使者慕容坦賜彌俄突雜彩六十匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the envoy Murong Tan to grant Mie'etuo sixty bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Murong Tan was ordered to give Mie'etuo sixty bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 宣武詔之曰：「卿遠據沙外，頻申誠款，覽捐忠志，特所欽嘉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu issued an edict to him: "You hold far dominion beyond the sands and have repeatedly shown good faith; reading your loyal intent, we especially admire you.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu wrote, "You rule far beyond the desert and have often proved your loyalty; we hold your devotion in special regard.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕、嚈噠、吐谷渾所以交通者，皆路由高昌，掎角相接。

translations.literal: The Rouran, Hephthalites, and Tuyuhun communicate with one another because all their routes pass through Gaochang, forming a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran, Hephthalites, and Tuyuhun traffic with one another along roads that all run through Gaochang, so their realms interlock like pincers.

sentences.zh: 今高昌內附，遣使迎引。

translations.literal: Now Gaochang has submitted inward and we are sending envoys to welcome and guide.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang has now submitted, and we are sending envoys to receive them.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕往來路絕，奸勢。

translations.literal: The Rouran routes of coming and going are cut off; treacherous power is checked.
translations.idiomatic: With the Rouran road severed, their treacherous designs are frustrated as well.

sentences.zh: 不得妄令群小敢有陵犯，擁塞王人，罪在不赦。」

translations.literal: You must not rashly let petty men dare to encroach or obstruct imperial envoys—the crime is unpardonable."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let petty chiefs harass or block the court's messengers—such offense will not be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 彌俄突尋與蠕蠕主伏圖戰于蒲類海北，為伏圖所敗，西走三百餘里。

translations.literal: Before long Mie'etuo fought the Rouran chief Futou north of the Pulei Sea and was defeated by Futou, fleeing west more than three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mie'etuo fought Futou of the Rouran north of the Pulei Sea, was beaten, and fled west over three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 伏圖次於伊吾北山。

translations.literal: Futou halted at the northern hills of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Futou camped on the northern hills of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 先是，高昌王麹嘉表求內徙，宣武遣孟威迎之。

translations.literal: Earlier the king of Gaochang, Qu Jia, had memorialized asking to move inward; Xuanwu sent Meng Wei to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier King Qu Jia of Gaochang had asked to migrate inward, and Xuanwu sent Meng Wei to escort him.

sentences.zh: 至伊吾，蠕蠕見威軍，怖而遁走。

translations.literal: Reaching Yiwu, the Rouran saw Wei's army and, afraid, fled away.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiwu the Rouran sighted the Wei host and fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 彌俄突聞其離駭；

translations.literal: Mie'etuo heard of their departure in alarm;
translations.idiomatic: Mie'etuo heard they had gone and seized the moment;

sentences.zh: 追擊大破之，殺伏圖于薄類海北，割其發，送于孟威。

translations.literal: he pursued, greatly defeated them, killed Futou north of the Pulei Sea, cut off his hair, and sent it to Meng Wei.
translations.idiomatic: he pursued, routed them utterly, slew Futou north of the Pulei Sea, and sent his hair to Meng Wei.

sentences.zh: 又遣使獻龍馬五匹，金、銀、貂皮及諸方物。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys presenting five dragon-horses and gold, silver, sable pelts, and other regional products.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys again with five dragon-steeds, gold, silver, sable, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔東城子於亮報之，賜樂器一部、樂工八十人、赤槹十匹，雜彩六十匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dongchengzi Yu Liang to reply, granting one set of musical instruments, eighty musicians, ten bolts of red staff-cloth, and sixty bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang of Dongcheng was sent to reply with instruments, eighty musicians, ten bolts of red cloth, and sixty of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 彌俄突遣其莫何去汾屋引叱賀真貢其方物。

translations.literal: Mie'etuo sent his Moguhu Fenwuyin Chihozhen to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Mie'etuo sent his minister Fenwuyin Chihozhen with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，彌俄突與蠕蠕主醜奴戰敗，被禽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign Mie'etuo was defeated in battle with the Rouran chief Chounu and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ming's reign Mie'etuo lost to the Rouran chief Chounu and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 醜奴系其兩腳于駑馬之上，頓曳殺之，漆其頭為飲器。

translations.literal: Chounu tied his two feet to a nag and dragged him to death, then lacquered his skull as a drinking cup.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu lashed his feet to a pony, dragged him until he died, and lacquered his skull for a cup.

sentences.zh: 其部眾悉入嚈噠。

translations.literal: His tribes all entered the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: His people passed entirely under Hephthalite rule.

sentences.zh: 經數年，嚈噠聽彌俄突弟伊匐還國。

translations.literal: After several years the Hephthalites allowed Mie'etuo's younger brother Yifu to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the Hephthalites let Mie'etuo's brother Yifu go home.

sentences.zh: 伊匐既復國，遣使奉表，於是詔遣使者谷楷等拜為鎮西將軍、西海郡開國公、高車王。

translations.literal: Once Yifu had restored his state he sent envoys with a memorial; thereupon an edict sent the envoy Gu Kai and others to invest him as General Who Guards the West, Duke Who Opens the Western Sea Commandery, and King of the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu then sent a memorial, and the court sent Gu Kai to invest him General Who Guards the West, Duke of Western Sea, and King of the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 伊匐復大破蠕蠕，蠕蠕主婆羅門走投涼州。

translations.literal: Yifu again greatly defeated the Rouran, and the Rouran chief Poluomen fled in defeat to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu routed the Rouran again, and their chief Poluomen fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 正光中，伊匐遣使朝貢，因乞硃畫步挽一乘並幔褥、鞦鹁必一副、傘扇各一枚、青曲蓋五枚、赤漆扇五枚、鼓角十枚，詔給之。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era Yifu sent envoys to court in tribute and begged one vermilion-painted hand-drawn carriage with curtains and cushions, one set of swing and pole gear, one parasol and one fan each, five blue curved canopies, five red-lacquered fans, and ten horns and drums; an edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang he sent tribute and asked for a painted carriage, hangings, swing gear, parasol, fans, canopies, lacquered fans, and drums—the court granted all.

sentences.zh: 伊匐後與蠕蠕戰，敗歸，其弟越居殺伊匐而自立。

translations.literal: Later Yifu fought the Rouran again, was defeated and returned; his younger brother Yueju killed Yifu and set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Later, defeated again by the Rouran, he was slain at home by his brother Yueju, who seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 天平中，越居復為蠕蠕所破，伊匐子比適復殺越居而自立。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era Yueju was again defeated by the Rouran; Yifu's son Bishi killed Yueju and set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping the Rouran broke Yueju, and Yifu's son Bishi killed him and became king.

sentences.zh: 興和中，比適又為蠕蠕所破，越居子去賓自蠕蠕奔東魏。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era Bishi was again defeated by the Rouran; Yueju's son Qubin fled from the Rouran to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe the Rouran defeated Bishi, and Yueju's son Qubin fled to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 齊神武欲招納遠人，上言封去賓為高車王，拜安北將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi, Shenwu, wished to win over distant peoples; he memorialized to enfeoff Qubin as King of the Gaoche and appoint him General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sought distant allies, had Qubin enfeoffed King of the Gaoche, and made him General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而病死。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 初，道武時有吐突鄰部在女水上，常與解如部相為脣齒，不供職事。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Daowu's time, the Tutuling tribe was on the Nüshui and often stood with the Jieru tribe as lip and teeth, refusing corvée duty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daowu's reign the Tutuling lived on the Nü River, allied with the Jieru, and refused service.

sentences.zh: 登國三年，道武親西征，度弱洛水，復西行趣其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dengguo Daowu personally campaigned west, crossed the Ruoluo River, and again marched west toward their state.
translations.idiomatic: In Dengguo year three Daowu marched west in person, crossed the Ruoluo, and pressed on toward their lands.

sentences.zh: 至女水上，討解如部落，破之。

translations.literal: Reaching the Nüshui he attacked the Jieru tribe and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Nü River he struck the Jieru and broke them.

sentences.zh: 明年春，盡略徙其部落畜產而還。

translations.literal: The next spring he wholly carried off their tribes and herds and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring he drove off their people and livestock and returned.

sentences.zh: 又有紇突鄰，與紇奚世同部落，而各有大人長帥，擁集種類，常為寇于意辛山，登國五年，道武勒眾親討焉。

translations.literal: There were also the Hetuling, of the same tribe as the Hexi in former ages but each with its own great chief; they gathered their kind and often raided at Yixin Mountain; in the fifth year of Dengguo Daowu led his host in person to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hetuling shared ancestry with the Hexi but kept separate chiefs; they raided Yixin Mountain until Dengguo year five, when Daowu attacked in person.

sentences.zh: 慕容駖率師來會，大破之。

translations.literal: Murong Lin led his army to join him and they were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin brought his troops to the rendezvous and they were shattered.

sentences.zh: 紇突鄰大人屋地鞬，紇奚大人庫寒等皆舉部歸降。

translations.literal: The Hetuling great chief Wudijian and the Hexi great chief Kuhan and others all led their tribes to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs Wudijian of the Hetuling and Kuhan of the Hexi submitted with their clans.

sentences.zh: 皇始二年，車駕伐中山，軍于柏肆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangshi the imperial carriage attacked Zhongshan and encamped at Baixi.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangshi year two the emperor besieged Zhongshan and camped at Baixi.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶夜來攻營，軍人驚，走還于國。

translations.literal: Murong Bao came by night to attack the camp; the soldiers were alarmed and fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao attacked by night; the army panicked and marched home.

sentences.zh: 路由并州，遂反，將攻晉陽，并州刺史元延討平之。

translations.literal: On the road through Bingzhou they rebelled and were about to attack Jinyang; Governor of Bingzhou Yuan Yan defeated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Bingzhou they rose in revolt against Jinyang until Governor Yuan Yan put them down.

sentences.zh: 紇突鄰部帥匿物尼、紇奚部帥叱奴根等復聚党反于陰館，南安西元順討之不克，死者數千人。

translations.literal: The Hetuling chief Niwuni and the Hexi chief Chinugen again gathered factions and rebelled at Yinguan; the Pacifier of the West Yuan Shun attacked them without success, and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Niwuni and Chinugen rebelled again at Yinguan; Yuan Shun failed to crush them and thousands fell.

sentences.zh: 道武聞之，遣安遠將軍庾岳還討匿物尼等，皆殄之。

translations.literal: When Daowu heard of it he sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Yu Yue back to attack Niwuni and the others and destroyed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu sent Yu Yue back, who exterminated Niwuni and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 又有侯呂鄰部，眾萬餘口，常依險畜牧。

translations.literal: There was also the Houlüling tribe, more than ten thousand mouths, who often pastured in defensible places.
translations.idiomatic: The Houlüling numbered more than ten thousand and pastured in strong country.

sentences.zh: 登國中，其大人叱伐為寇於苦水河。

translations.literal: In the middle of the Dengguo era their great chief Chifa raided along the Kushui River.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Dengguo their chief Chifa raided the Kushui.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，道武大破之，並禽其別帥焉古延等。

translations.literal: In the eighth summer Daowu greatly defeated them and also captured their sub-chief Yanguyan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year eight Daowu routed them and took the sub-chief Yanguyan.

sentences.zh: 薛幹部常屯聚於三城之間，及滅衛辰後，其部帥太悉伏望軍歸順，道武撫安之。

translations.literal: The Xiegan tribe often gathered between the Three Cities; after the destruction of Wei Chen their chief Taisifu saw the army and submitted; Daowu comforted and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiegan held the Three Cities until, after Wei Chen fell, chief Taisifu submitted and Daowu received him.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，衛辰子屈丐奔其部。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Wei Chen's son Qubugai fled to their tribe.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return, Qubugai son of Wei Chen fled to the Xiegan.

sentences.zh: 道武聞之，使使詔太悉伏執送之。

translations.literal: Daowu heard of it and sent an envoy ordering Taisifu to seize and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu sent orders for Taisifu to seize and hand him over.

sentences.zh: 太悉伏出屈丐以示使者曰：「今窮而見投，寧與俱亡，何忍送之！」

translations.literal: Taisifu brought Qubugai out to show the envoy and said: "Now in extremity he has come to me—how could I let him perish together with me and bear to send him away?"
translations.idiomatic: Taisifu produced Qubugai and told the envoy, "He comes to me in ruin—I will die with him rather than betray him."

sentences.zh: 遂不遣。

translations.literal: He would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to surrender him.

sentences.zh: 道武大怒，車駕親討之。

translations.literal: Daowu was greatly angered and the imperial carriage personally campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu raged and marched against him in person.

sentences.zh: 會太悉伏先出擊曹覆寅，官軍乘虛，遂屠其城，獲太悉伏妻子、珍寶，徙其人而還。

translations.literal: It happened that Taisifu had gone out first to strike Cao Fuyin; the army took advantage of the emptiness, sacked his city, took Taisifu's wife, children, and treasure, and moved his people back.
translations.idiomatic: Taisifu was away attacking Cao Fuyin; the Wei army took his city, his family and wealth, and relocated his people.

sentences.zh: 太悉伏來赴不及，送奔姚興。

translations.literal: Taisifu came too late and, unable to catch up, sent himself to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Taisifu returned too late and fled to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，亡歸嶺北。

translations.literal: Before long he died and returned to the north of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died on the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 上郡以西諸鮮卑、雜胡聞而皆應之。

translations.literal: All the Xianbei and mixed Hu west of Shang commandery heard of it and responded.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei and other Hu west of Shang commandery rose at the news.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年，屈丐盡劫掠總服之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxi Qubugai plundered all who submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi year five Qubugai ravaged every tribe that had submitted.

sentences.zh: 及平統萬，薛幹種類皆得為編戶矣。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified the Xiegan clans were all entered into the household registers.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongwan fell the Xiegan were registered as common households.

sentences.zh: 而牽屯山鮮卑別種破多蘭部世傳主部落。

translations.literal: Among the Xianbei of Qiantun Mountain the Poduolan branch had from of old held lordship over the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: On Qiantun Mountain the Poduolan Xianbei had long ruled their branch.

sentences.zh: 至木易幹，有武力壯勇，劫掠左右，西及金城，東侵安定，數年間，諸種患之。

translations.literal: At Muyigan there was martial strength and valor; he plundered all about, west to Jincheng and east into Anding; within several years the various tribes suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Muyigan was strong and bold, raiding west to Jincheng and east into Anding until the tribes groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 天興四年，遣常山王遵討之于高平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxing the court sent Prince of Changshan Zun to attack him at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing year four Prince Zun of Changshan was sent against him at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 木易幹將數千騎棄國遁走，盡徙其人于京師、餘種分迸，其後，為赫連屈丐所滅。

translations.literal: Muyigan led several thousand horse, abandoned his state, and fled; his people were wholly moved to the capital, the remnant clans scattered, and later they were destroyed by Helian Qubugai.
translations.idiomatic: Muyigan fled with a few thousand horse; his people were moved to the capital, the remnant scattered, and Helian Qubugai later wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 又黜弗、素古延等諸部，富而不恭。

translations.literal: The Chufu, Suguyan, and other tribes were rich yet disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: The Chufu and Suguyan were wealthy but insolent.

sentences.zh: 天興五年，材官將軍和突率六千騎襲而獲之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing the Master of Works He Tu led six thousand horse in a surprise attack and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing year five He Tu surprised them with six thousand horse and took them captive.

sentences.zh: 又越勤倍泥部，永興五年，轉牧跋那山西。

translations.literal: There was also the Yueqinbeini tribe; in the fifth year of Yongxing they moved their herds west of Mount Bana.
translations.idiomatic: The Yueqinbeini moved their herds west of Mount Bana in Yongxing year five.

sentences.zh: 七月，遣奚斤討破之，徙其人而還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Xi Jin was sent to defeat them and their people were moved back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xi Jin defeated them and resettled the captives.

sentences.zh: 論曰：周之獫狁，漢之匈奴。

translations.literal: The historians comment: The Xianyun of Zhou, the Xiongnu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: the Xianyun of Zhou were the Xiongnu of Han.

sentences.zh: 其作害中國，故久矣。

translations.literal: Their harm to China is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Their raids on China are ancient.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之世，種族瓜分，去來沙漠之陲，窺擾鄣塞之際，猶皆東胡之緒余，冒頓之枝葉。

translations.literal: In the Wei and Jin eras the tribes were carved apart, coming and going on the desert marches and peering at the barrier passes—yet all were threads of the Eastern Hu, branches of Modun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin the tribes split and wandered the desert edge, probing the frontier—yet all sprang from the Eastern Hu and Modun's line.

sentences.zh: 至如蠕蠕者，匈奴之裔，根本莫尋，逃形集醜，自小為大，風馳鳥赴，倏來忽往，代京由之屢駭，戎車所以不寧。

translations.literal: As for the Rouran, descendants of the Xiongnu whose roots cannot be traced, they hid their forms and gathered villains, growing from small to great; like wind-driven birds they came and went in a flash, so that the capital was repeatedly alarmed and the war chariots knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran, Xiongnu kin of unknown origin, gathered outcasts and swelled from nothing; they swept in like birds on the wind, again and again terrifying the capital and keeping the armies uneasy.

sentences.zh: 是故魏氏祖宗，揚威曜武，驅其畜產，收其部落，翦之窮發之野，逐之無人之鄉。

translations.literal: Therefore the Wei founders displayed might and martial glory, drove off their herds, gathered their tribes, cut them down in the uttermost wilds, and chased them into trackless country.
translations.idiomatic: So the Wei founders flung out their power, seized herds and tribes, cut them down in the farthest wilds, and drove them into empty lands.

sentences.zh: 豈好肆兵極銳，凶器不戢？

translations.literal: Was it that they loved to wield arms to the utmost and would not sheathe cruel weapons?
translations.idiomatic: Was it love of war and the sword left forever bare?

sentences.zh: 蓋亦急病除惡，事不得已。

translations.literal: Rather it was urgent illness requiring the removal of evil—the affair could not be helped.
translations.idiomatic: No—they fought as one fights a grave sickness, because there was no choice.

sentences.zh: 其狡狄強弱之由，猾虜服叛之跡，故備錄云。

translations.literal: The reasons for the strength and weakness of these cunning Di and the traces of how such crafty barbarians submitted and rebelled are therefore set forth in full here.
translations.idiomatic: The rise and fall of these peoples and the record of their submission and revolt are therefore given here in full.
